docs.text: AeroGrid AeroGrid is a configurable 4 x 4 glass-cockpit dashboard for EdgeTX color radios. YAML layouts combine telemetry, model timers, flight tracking, switch states, trim positions, and model images in responsive panels. Use Documentation version in the header to match your installed release. main (unreleased) describes the development version. START HERE Install or upgrade AeroGrid Connect your radio and follow the guide to put AeroGrid on its SD card. Open Install / Upgrade → Before you start Color-screen radio (e.g., TX16S, TX15, GX15, T16/T18) EdgeTX 2.11 or later USB data cable Choose a guide For pilots and radio owners User Guide Install AeroGrid, create a dashboard, customize it, and troubleshoot common issues. Start with the User Guide → For specific answers Reference Guide Look up panel behavior, settings, and the layout YAML format. Browse the reference → For developers Developer Guide Build and test AeroGrid, learn the architecture, and contribute. Explore development → The complete Default layout at native 480 x 272 resolution, captured in the EdgeTX TX16S simulator using the production Modern Dark theme. Telemetry, transmitter voltage, and switch positions are sample inputs; the timer and global variables use isolated firmware model settings. AeroGrid at the flying field. Modern Dark on a RadioMaster TX16S. Modern Light on the same radio. Why AeroGrid? EdgeTX is an excellent foundation: open source, remarkably configurable, and flexible enough to support a wide range of radios and aircraft. AeroGrid builds on those strengths rather than replacing them. The dashboard experience has not always matched that flexibility. Many widgets have a dated appearance, and mixing widgets from different authors often means mixing different fonts, colors, spacing, and alarm styles. Individually useful widgets do not necessarily add up to a coherent interface. Earlier graphics APIs made polished, consistent interfaces harder to build. With LVGL, EdgeTX now offers a more flexible foundation for a shared UI design system. Projects such as Kyle Stacy's KSE Dashboards for Rotorflight helicopters show what focused dashboards can offer. For fixed-wing pilots, however, options for a modern, cohesive dashboard that can be freely rearranged remain limited. AeroGrid's goal is to provide flexible, configurable, modern-looking dashboards and panels , with a consistent visual language throughout. Choose the information that matters to your model, arrange it in a YAML-defined grid, and keep the same typography, spacing, colors, and state indicators across the dashboard. How to use Follow these three short walkthroughs to install AeroGrid , create a dashboard, and customize it. Install AeroGrid Read the installation guide or watch on YouTube . Create an Empty dashboard Read the setup guide or watch on YouTube . Add, move, and resize panels Read the editing guide or watch on YouTube .

docs.text: Repository and architecture Start with main.lua for host behavior, an existing panel for presentation, or a service for data acquisition. AeroGrid runs as one EdgeTX widget ; the dashboard's panels are modules managed by that widget, not separate EdgeTX widgets. Find your way around Path What belongs here src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/main.lua EdgeTX entry points, native options, event routing, and callback scheduling. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/lib/ Layout parsing/storage, grid geometry, panel hosting, shared services, rendering primitives, themes, and editor modules. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/panels/ Thirteen user-facing panel types plus host-diagnostics , service-probe , and the fixed-data theme-showcase . src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/ Shipped layouts. tests/fixtures/layouts/development/ Simulator and review layouts used by tests and disposable SD images. src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/assets/ Runtime editor icon and its license. tests/unit/ Focused module and panel tests. tests/integration/ Host, editor, dashboard, budget, and resource tests using mocked EdgeTX. tests/support/ Assertions, firmware-aware EdgeTX/LVGL mocks, and widget/layout fixture helpers. tests/fixtures/ Deterministic simulator SD card, test-only panels, and test layouts. tools/ Release packaging, native screenshots, capture recipes, and Python tooling tests. docs/ Website sources, reference pages, reviewed images, and hardware evidence. .vscode/ TX16S profile and build/test tasks; local settings are ignored. .github/workflows/ CI, documentation publication, and manual release workflow. plans/ Design specifications and planning material, not runtime input. build/ Ignored, generated output; never the source of truth. The project specification provides design background. Check the implementation and its tests for exact current signatures; planning examples can describe earlier contracts. Follow a dashboard from disk to display EdgeTX loads main.lua and passes a zone and the native Layout and Theme options. Layout choices use stable positions maintained by layout_registry.lua . Stable layout positions are stored in /AEROGRID/layout-registry.txt , separately from /AEROGRID/theme-registry.txt . The host resolves the selected name through layout_store.lua . A saved /AEROGRID/layouts/<name>.yaml takes precedence over the bundled /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/<name>.yaml ; a missing file can fall back to Default . yaml.lua tokenizes the constrained YAML format; layout.lua validates version, grid, placements, and configuration. grid.lua turns zero-based positions and spans in the 4 x 4 grid into pixel rectangles. The host loads services and panel modules, checks compatibility, resolves typed settings, and creates each panel inside its own LVGL container. Foreground/background callbacks update subscribed services and dispatch panel work. A zone or fullscreen change triggers bounded reflow rather than reconstructing every object in a single frame. Host coordination has three boundaries: Module Ownership dashboard_loader.lua Layout recovery, staged parsing, service/panel construction, and placement-local services. dashboard_lifecycle.lua Empty-page decoration, batched reflow, fullscreen-to-App rebuilds, and page retirement/replacement. editor_controller.lua Editor activation, staged advancement, dashboard previews, draft restoration, and adoption after saving. Their new functions bind host operations once per widget. They do not capture another widget's context or introduce per-refresh forwarding wrappers. main.lua decides which operation advances; loading and cleanup keep their explicit stages. Page retirement and replacement run in separate callbacks so deferred cleanup cannot invalidate objects belonging to the replacement page. Panels use container-local coordinates. They must not draw at absolute screen coordinates or assume the TX16S's dimensions. The host reserves the same top-left footprint for the native App-mode menu and fullscreen AeroGrid menu. Use the shared geometry instead of adding panel-specific menu offsets. lib/package.lua records package, runtime API, panel API, and layout versions. The current layout schema is version 5. The central layout module keeps an adjacent migration registry: each source version provides a header step and a panel step for that version-to-next-version transition. A future version must add every intervening step; a layout is rejected if its source version is newer or any transition is missing. Runtime loading validates the header, applies at most one header transition per loader callback, then parses each panel and applies at most one panel transition per callback before validating and building that panel. Staged Save follows the same bounded progression, keeping header migration, each panel migration, validation, and persistence in separate callbacks. The synchronous whole-layout helpers are for tests and tools, not runtime callback paths. Loading changes only the in-memory document and emits an upgrade notice; only explicit editor Save persists the current schema. Runtime modules expose RUNTIME_API ; panels expose apiVersion . The host surfaces incompatible modules and isolates failures where possible. These checks detect incompatible mixtures, not every stale or mixed package: deploy the complete widget directory. Shared services own firmware reads Panels subscribe in create , retain read-only snapshots, and render them. They do not each poll EdgeTX or maintain their own telemetry cache. Subscriptions to the same source share polling, and an unsubscribed service does not consume scheduled work. Service module Responsibility telemetry_service.lua Source resolution, readings, units, precision, freshness, and link status. model_service.lua Model identity/image, timers, flight mode, and TX voltage. control_service.lua Trims, final channel outputs and their trim associations, switch conditions, GV snapshots, and verified GV9 FM0 increments. armed_service.lua Saved model Armed precedence, legacy switch fallback, and immutable effective arm views over shared Control polls. flight_service.lua Shared model-flight detection, once-only count, optional Sticky output, and timestamped boundaries. smart_flight.lua Optional protocol-identified flight sensors with per-sensor receipt/freshness and SI units. extrema_service.lua Sensor extrema and dashboard flight-session tracking. navigation_service.lua GPS fix, pilot/home position, distance, and north-up bearing. history_service.lua Error-bounded chart recordings, cumulative recording time, flight boundaries, raw extrema, line-only smoothing, and bounded rolling expiration. services.lua Environment/snapshots, subscription registration, and bounded scheduling/update dispatch. Snapshots are read-only views over service-owned state, mutated in place by the service to avoid per-frame allocations. Missing APIs, unknown sources, and missing fixes yield unavailable data; panel code must handle that explicitly. services.addSubscription publishes an entry's live view and records its polling order/count. Each domain service still owns name lookup, duplicate detection, source resolution, and its polling metadata. Link/session-only subscriptions remain separate from source polling lists. Telemetry zero is not inherently unavailable. EdgeTX can return zero both for a real reading and for a stopped stream. AeroGrid preserves the last live value when an ambiguous zero arrives with a down link, but accepts a live zero. getRSSI() is not reliable for every protocol; the service can stop trusting it when a non-zero source proves that telemetry is arriving. Staleness is link-wide, not per sensor, and a configured but never-received sensor can appear as valid zero on a live link. Local switch values remain usable without a receiver. Chart history observes completed telemetry polls rather than reading changed revisions during redraw: unchanged numeric samples still occupy recording time, and raw spikes must not be lost between frames. Observer failures are isolated from telemetry polling and reported through normal service failure handling. services.armed:state() describes the saved model condition; :state(legacySwitch) resolves model-over-legacy precedence for a consumer. Snapshots expose condition , key , origin , generation , configured , available , fresh , updatedAt , Boolean value , revision , and status . An unavailable/stale reading is not disarmed. Reliability is evaluated on access with a one-second maximum sample age, so a failed poller cannot leave a permanently fresh reading. revision changes on observed sample/reliability changes; generation changes when the widget runtime is rebuilt. status is unconfigured , ready , or unavailable ; invalid configuration is reported through normal host error isolation. The resolver owns no separate polling work: Control still reads each switch once per runtime. Configuration is model-wide; each dashboard publishes its own view over that same condition. History and extrema key sessions by the effective condition. A configured model Armed unifies their arm inputs; absent model arming retains independent legacy switches. Each chart arm configuration has its own cumulative session. It pauses on disarm unless a matching shared flight is still active, including its disarm grace, and resumes the same recording; geometry reflow keeps it, while rebuilding the service runtime clears it. Each source/options subscription stores at most 6,144 connected linear knots. A fixed-anchor slope corridor chooses synthesized shared endpoints within half a displayed precision step of every observed value (filtered values if EMA is enabled). Numerical margin is reserved before accepting a segment; when that margin consumes the tolerance, exact native values are retained. Unknown sensor precision uses the strictest supported tolerance until discovery completes. Knots use chunked <I4n / <I4j packing: cumulative recording ticks with gap/type bits and a lossless native Lua float or integer. Payload is 48 KiB per full recording on float32 firmware, or 72 KiB on double-precision hosts, excluding string/table/index and rendering overhead. Matching armed-switch/source/options subscriptions share storage. Absolute first / last sequence IDs and scalar history:point reads avoid per-knot snapshot tables. Growing history freezes at capacity without relaxing accuracy; rolling expiration reuses ring slots while retaining an interpolation anchor. Raw readouts/extrema continue even when plot storage is full. Multilevel extrema/gap indexes accelerate projection only inside one pixel column; they never replace stored knots. Projection, native trace updates and gap-marker updates are staged with bounded work per callback. Geometry changes restart pending projection. Recorded gaps stay separate except when their endpoints coincide on screen; marker objects are pooled by pixel column. Unchanged readouts are cached so their callback budget can process a larger bounded projection batch; same-pixel extrema do not add redundant geometry. History consumes at most one flight journal record per service turn, keyed by the event's pinned armKey , never by the optional Sticky output or the current broker arm. Per effective arm, 128 recording spans map wall-clock at timestamps to the cumulative recording axis; qualification/confirmation receipt times do not place boundaries. Grace samples remain after the mapped end. A 64-interval ring supplies scalar history:flight(sessionView, index) reads, independent of metric subscriptions. Shaded flight bands are staged in a bounded native-object pool behind the grid and traces. Each chart snapshots its inputs and stages a complete plot in a second reusable buffer before swapping it on screen. Arm/disarm triangles use a bounded directional transition journal. A separate resume journal drives fixed-width axis gaps and dotted trace connectors; the same projection maps traces, flight bands, grid lines, and axis markers. Crowded gaps evict the oldest visible section rather than narrowing the gaps. During normal sampling, flight bands clip to the recorded telemetry horizon. Telemetry-sampling turns reserve projection headroom without lowering the existing callback or staged-drain limits. Journal loss sets the session's flightLost flag and closes an unmatched open band at its last observed recording time rather than extending it into later flights. Late attachment can recover the current active interval only from its recorded portion; old completed flights do not create new history. Model epochs clear intervals and mapping spans. Draft chart previews read compatible live views through a read-only facade and make no live subscriptions. Compatible previews can become live panels after saving without losing history; new or incompatible subscriptions require a post-save rebuild. Shared flight tracking The factory-scoped broker in flight_service.lua owns a separate non-UI Control/Telemetry runtime and optional Smart sensor poller. Any live widget callback can pump it. Dashboard registrations are weakly held; rebuilds mark proposals pending before replacing them. Unanimous effective arm/configuration proposals are required, not the first caller's settings. Saved model Armed overrides every declaration. A qualified session pins its arm, detector settings, and output until completion, including output cleanup when proposals change or conflict. Counter panels only render state. services.flight:state() is an immutable live view. It exposes model/epoch, configuration revision/status, phase ( ground , starting , active , ending ), active , flight ID/count, candidate/qualification/disarm/completion timestamps, qualification reason and smartStatus , and actionable diagnostics. ready describes configuration, not telemetry validity. Unknown/stale arm observations never confirm disarm. services.flight:boundaries(afterSequence, epoch) returns immutable records, the oldest retained sequence, and a gap flag. The journal retains 64 start/end records with epoch, sequence, flight ID/count, pinned armKey , kind , at , observedAt , and qualification reason ( standard , smart-altitude , or smart-speed ). Start at is the motor candidate start; end at is the final disarm start. observedAt is qualification or completion, so duration excludes the disarm grace. Consumers must reconcile a gap or changed epoch; they must never read Sticky output as their event bus. Smart shortcuts use the same qualification/effect path; they do not move the candidate timestamp. The standard timer remains an independent OR path. Model flight.smartDetection defaults false. Smart requires EdgeTX getSourceValue receipt/current/fresh flags, not getValue zeros or link-wide freshness. Firmware isFresh spans roughly 160-320 ms; isCurrent only means the sensor is not marked old and may remain true for seconds after updates stop. Numeric receipt timestamps are not exposed. Smart bridges current finite readings for at most 1.2 seconds after positive per-sensor isFresh evidence; polling a cached value never renews that evidence. Never-received, old, unavailable, invalid, or expired data invalidate immediately. A shortcut can finish only once renewed evidence from every required source spans the full two-second hold; a cached value alone cannot finish it. Continuity counters preserve invalidations between detector ticks. This supports healthy 500ms/1s streams without treating the short fresh flag as a minimum update rate. Receipt age remains bounded evidence, not an exact timestamp or instant stopped-stream detector. Callbacks too infrequent to observe fresh flags conservatively fall back to standard detection. The Smart poller is due every 100ms. Ordinary chart callbacks continue on Smart polling callbacks: the host reduces that callback's dashboard telemetry batch from eight sources to four, reserving room for Smart's four sensor categories. Both pollers retain round-robin progress; Smart does not skip whole chart callbacks. Selected metadata is compared directly rather than rebuilding identity strings on every poll. Expensive loading/editor work still gets separate, per-widget fair slices, and pending input takes priority. Discovery uses numeric telemN sources and custom sensor metadata from model.getSensor , never names or units alone. Supported single-module families are CRSF (including ELRS) and native FrSky S.Port; unknown/MULTI or multiple active modules fall back rather than guessing. CRSF barometric altitude is ID 0x09 /instance 0; GPS position, groundspeed, and satellite count are ID 0x02 /instances 0, 2, and 5. S.Port uses the firmware barometric/GPS position/groundspeed ID ranges, with matching GPS/speed instances. Calculated sensors and GPS altitude are excluded. Ambiguous categories are disabled independently. GPS requires fresh valid coordinates/delay and, on CRSF, at least four fresh satellites. Numeric inputs reject nonfinite values and normalize metres/feet and knots/m/s/ft/s/km/h/mph. Altitude references require an observed disarmed-to-armed transition using a recent sample explicitly witnessed while disarmed, or fresh evidence at that transition. Merely current late readings never rebase an armed session. Motor interruptions preserve the reference but reset holds; unknown arm resets holds without inventing disarm. Metadata changes and scheduling gaps invalidate the reference conservatively. Fixed shortcuts are strictly above +3 m or 10 mph for at least 200 ticks, allowing only precision-scaled conversion roundoff (including float32 firmware). smartStatus explains fallback in the native Model settings dialog; confirmed field changes persist and update live detection immediately. Model settings use their own schema/revision and losslessly encoded model filename under /AEROGRID/models/ . Saves verify model identity and revision before verified file replacement. Layout saves and previews never write this document. Legacy detector declarations remain compatible until model settings are changed; retained arm metadata stays with its layout rather than becoming model-wide Armed. Schema version 1 has an optional top-level armed condition: missing preserves per-consumer legacy fallback, while "" explicitly disables arming, including fallbacks. Nonempty values must be physical positions or logical switches L01–L64 (optionally inverted). Numeric channel IDs are rejected. The model document is loaded in a separate callback before Armed and panel construction. Saving a different arm condition rebuilds every registered dashboard and clears captured homes, preserving layout data and a pinned active flight's completion/cleanup. Previous per-widget Armed selections are never silently promoted; conflicting old selections require an explicit model choice. The optional top-level sessionReset uses the same switch syntax; missing or "" disables it. A shared control poller detects false-to-true transitions independently of flight detection. Activation advances the flight epoch, cancels detection, releases its owned output, and stages every dashboard's reload with captured homes cleared and editor drafts retained. Counting waits for a fresh disarm observation. Model changes also reset the flight epoch; ordinary dashboard rebuilds do not. Add or change a panel Use panels/flight-mode.lua as a small working example and lib/panel_host.lua as the authoritative contract. Declaration or callback Role id , apiVersion , supportedSpans Identify the module, check compatibility, and advertise valid grid sizes. settings Typed fields, defaults, bounds, and choices used by validation and the editor. refreshInterval Desired foreground interval in 10 ms ticks; work still shares the host budget. refreshCost Whole-number share of the six host refresh slots (default 1). Chart uses all six so dense layouts cannot batch expensive redraws into one callback. create(parent, rect, settings, services) Build LVGL objects, subscribe to data, and return private instance state. refresh(context) Optional callback to update existing objects from snapshots. May return a whole-number interval of 1–6000 ticks; nil preserves the current interval. A second result of true reserves subsequent turns among panels of the same type until the update completes; other panel types and services continue running. update(context, rect, settings, detailsOnly, placement) Optional geometry/configuration update. Host reflows and editor resizes pass the current grid placement as the fifth argument, leaving the internal detailsOnly argument unset. background(context) Optional work when the dashboard is not visible. event(context, event) Optional event handling; return true when consumed. destroy(context) Optional cleanup of panel-owned references. validateSettings(settings, span, config) Optional cross-field and span-dependent validation. Put the module at panels/<type>.lua and reference that type in a layout. Regular panels declare supportedSpans = { "any" } and adapt their contents to every in-bounds span of the 4 x 4 grid. Use an explicit span list when there is a real rendering constraint: Host diagnostics and Service probe need at least 2x2, Chart needs a wide or square placement at least 2x1, while Theme showcase requires 4x4. Declare only spans you actually render correctly. A list setting ( type = "table" ) declares entry fields with keys or nested paths, labels, types, and appropriate defaults/bounds/choices. The editor uses this schema to offer even fields omitted from the YAML, and can remove cleared optional fields. List declarations, including nested lists, can set itemLabel to a singular name such as "Metric" or "State" . The editor names rows using the first nonempty label or source, then itemLabel and the one-based index; lists without itemLabel use "Entry" . Do not build a separate settings UI for each panel. The public theme.lua API composes palette/state resolution with typography.lua (measurement, font fitting, unit metrics) and panel_layout.lua (frames, slots, bands, and regions). The public primitives.lua API composes LVGL objects with reading.lua (reading/unit composition, redraw detection, and visibility/reflow reconciliation). Installed functions are direct references, not per-call wrappers; each widget has its own caches and mutable API tables. The host supplies these dependencies when executing the modules. Pure-Lua tests use tests/support/module_loader.lua to compose the same APIs without installing firmware globals. Use theme.lua for bands, font fitting, shared colors, and spacing, and primitives.lua for reusable LVGL objects. primitives.reading constructs the matching value/unit arrangement used by the battery and link readouts; optional units and differing initial geometry remain panel-specific. Keep a reading's font stable as its value changes, using the widest expected representation to choose it. When changing settings vocabulary or rendering, inspect sibling panels so the same setting retains the same meaning. Add focused tests, an integration case at every declared span, a simulator review layout when useful, and a panel reference page . If adding screenshot support, add a capture recipe and adapter as described in Project tools . Editor and persistence editor.lua owns draft operations; editor_ui.lua and editor_drawer.lua present them; editor_controller.lua coordinates them with the live dashboard. layout_store.lua handles saving, backups, and user-versus-shipped resolution; layout_registry.lua maintains name-to-choice positions. Keep these boundaries intact when changing save behavior. Panel settings drawers, including entry subdrawers, put Label first when declared, preserving the declaration order of all remaining controls. Editing does not overwrite bundled layouts. Save writes to /AEROGRID/layouts/ , and Save As creates a named user layout. The layout registry is initialized at script load, so new names require a restart before appearing in the native Layout picker. Save errors must preserve the draft and report failure. Test persistence through the store/editor suites, not just the visible dialog. Firmware constraints that affect design EdgeTX limits a widget callback to 20,000 Lua VM instructions . Creation, parsing, panel building, reload, and reflow are staged across callbacks. Services have bounded subscription updates, and panel work is capped and phase-staggered. Do not replace this with one synchronous "simpler" loader. The budget tests require strictly less than 75% of the callback allowance. Avoid object churn and retained callbacks. Shared labels install a persistent font callback; change its backing state through primitives.setFont rather than replacing the callback during refresh/reflow. Replacement retained Lua registry references in EdgeTX 2.12.4. Other firmware details already have helpers and regression coverage: theme.measureText uses lcd.sizeText where available and estimates otherwise; trim sources do not identify their axis, image decode failure is not reported by lvgl.image , and lvgl.arc positions use the center rather than the bounding-box corner. Reuse the existing panel logic, file checks, and primitives.arcBounds instead of introducing alternate assumptions.

Snapshots are read-only views over service-owned state, mutated in place by the service to avoid per-frame allocations. Missing APIs, unknown sources, and missing fixes yield unavailable data; panel code must handle that explicitly. services.addSubscription publishes an entry's live view and records its polling order/count. Each domain service still owns name lookup, duplicate detection, source resolution, and its polling metadata. Link/session-only subscriptions remain separate from source polling lists. Telemetry zero is not inherently unavailable. EdgeTX can return zero both for a real reading and for a stopped stream. AeroGrid preserves the last live value when an ambiguous zero arrives with a down link, but accepts a live zero. getRSSI() is not reliable for every protocol; the service can stop trusting it when a non-zero source proves that telemetry is arriving. Staleness is link-wide, not per sensor, and a configured but never-received sensor can appear as valid zero on a live link. Local switch values remain usable without a receiver. Chart history observes completed telemetry polls rather than reading changed revisions during redraw: unchanged numeric samples still occupy recording time, and raw spikes must not be lost between frames. Observer failures are isolated from telemetry polling and reported through normal service failure handling. services.armed:state() describes the saved model condition; :state(legacySwitch) resolves model-over-legacy precedence for a consumer. Snapshots expose condition , key , origin , generation , configured , available , fresh , updatedAt , Boolean value , revision , and status . An unavailable/stale reading is not disarmed. Reliability is evaluated on access with a one-second maximum sample age, so a failed poller cannot leave a permanently fresh reading. revision changes on observed sample/reliability changes; generation changes when the widget runtime is rebuilt. status is unconfigured , ready , or unavailable ; invalid configuration is reported through normal host error isolation. The resolver owns no separate polling work: Control still reads each switch once per runtime. Configuration is model-wide; each dashboard publishes its own view over that same condition. History and extrema key sessions by the effective condition. A configured model Armed unifies their arm inputs; absent model arming retains independent legacy switches. Each chart arm configuration has its own cumulative session. It pauses on disarm unless a matching shared flight is still active, including its disarm grace, and resumes the same recording; geometry reflow keeps it, while rebuilding the service runtime clears it. Each source/options subscription stores at most 6,144 connected linear knots. A fixed-anchor slope corridor chooses synthesized shared endpoints within half a displayed precision step of every observed value (filtered values if EMA is enabled). Numerical margin is reserved before accepting a segment; when that margin consumes the tolerance, exact native values are retained. Unknown sensor precision uses the strictest supported tolerance until discovery completes. Knots use chunked <I4n / <I4j packing: cumulative recording ticks with gap/type bits and a lossless native Lua float or integer. Payload is 48 KiB per full recording on float32 firmware, or 72 KiB on double-precision hosts, excluding string/table/index and rendering overhead. Matching armed-switch/source/options subscriptions share storage. Absolute first / last sequence IDs and scalar history:point reads avoid per-knot snapshot tables. Growing history freezes at capacity without relaxing accuracy; rolling expiration reuses ring slots while retaining an interpolation anchor. Raw readouts/extrema continue even when plot storage is full. Multilevel extrema/gap indexes accelerate projection only inside one pixel column; they never replace stored knots. Projection, native trace updates and gap-marker updates are staged with bounded work per callback. Geometry changes restart pending projection. Recorded gaps stay separate except when their endpoints coincide on screen; marker objects are pooled by pixel column. Unchanged readouts are cached so their callback budget can process a larger bounded projection batch; same-pixel extrema do not add redundant geometry. History consumes at most one flight journal record per service turn, keyed by the event's pinned armKey , never by the optional Sticky output or the current broker arm. Per effective arm, 128 recording spans map wall-clock at timestamps to the cumulative recording axis; qualification/confirmation receipt times do not place boundaries. Grace samples remain after the mapped end. A 64-interval ring supplies scalar history:flight(sessionView, index) reads, independent of metric subscriptions. Shaded flight bands are staged in a bounded native-object pool behind the grid and traces. Each chart snapshots its inputs and stages a complete plot in a second reusable buffer before swapping it on screen. Arm/disarm triangles use a bounded directional transition journal. A separate resume journal drives fixed-width axis gaps and dotted trace connectors; the same projection maps traces, flight bands, grid lines, and axis markers. Crowded gaps evict the oldest visible section rather than narrowing the gaps. During normal sampling, flight bands clip to the recorded telemetry horizon. Telemetry-sampling turns reserve projection headroom without lowering the existing callback or staged-drain limits. Journal loss sets the session's flightLost flag and closes an unmatched open band at its last observed recording time rather than extending it into later flights. Late attachment can recover the current active interval only from its recorded portion; old completed flights do not create new history. Model epochs clear intervals and mapping spans. Draft chart previews read compatible live views through a read-only facade and make no live subscriptions. Compatible previews can become live panels after saving without losing history; new or incompatible subscriptions require a post-save rebuild.

docs.text: The factory-scoped broker in flight_service.lua owns a separate non-UI Control/Telemetry runtime and optional Smart sensor poller. Any live widget callback can pump it. Dashboard registrations are weakly held; rebuilds mark proposals pending before replacing them. Unanimous effective arm/configuration proposals are required, not the first caller's settings. Saved model Armed overrides every declaration. A qualified session pins its arm, detector settings, and output until completion, including output cleanup when proposals change or conflict. Counter panels only render state. services.flight:state() is an immutable live view. It exposes model/epoch, configuration revision/status, phase ( ground , starting , active , ending ), active , flight ID/count, candidate/qualification/disarm/completion timestamps, qualification reason and smartStatus , and actionable diagnostics. ready describes configuration, not telemetry validity. Unknown/stale arm observations never confirm disarm. services.flight:boundaries(afterSequence, epoch) returns immutable records, the oldest retained sequence, and a gap flag. The journal retains 64 start/end records with epoch, sequence, flight ID/count, pinned armKey , kind , at , observedAt , and qualification reason ( standard , smart-altitude , or smart-speed ). Start at is the motor candidate start; end at is the final disarm start. observedAt is qualification or completion, so duration excludes the disarm grace. Consumers must reconcile a gap or changed epoch; they must never read Sticky output as their event bus. Smart shortcuts use the same qualification/effect path; they do not move the candidate timestamp. The standard timer remains an independent OR path. Model flight.smartDetection defaults false. Smart requires EdgeTX getSourceValue receipt/current/fresh flags, not getValue zeros or link-wide freshness. Firmware isFresh spans roughly 160-320 ms; isCurrent only means the sensor is not marked old and may remain true for seconds after updates stop. Numeric receipt timestamps are not exposed. Smart bridges current finite readings for at most 1.2 seconds after positive per-sensor isFresh evidence; polling a cached value never renews that evidence. Never-received, old, unavailable, invalid, or expired data invalidate immediately. A shortcut can finish only once renewed evidence from every required source spans the full two-second hold; a cached value alone cannot finish it. Continuity counters preserve invalidations between detector ticks. This supports healthy 500ms/1s streams without treating the short fresh flag as a minimum update rate. Receipt age remains bounded evidence, not an exact timestamp or instant stopped-stream detector. Callbacks too infrequent to observe fresh flags conservatively fall back to standard detection. The Smart poller is due every 100ms. Ordinary chart callbacks continue on Smart polling callbacks: the host reduces that callback's dashboard telemetry batch from eight sources to four, reserving room for Smart's four sensor categories. Both pollers retain round-robin progress; Smart does not skip whole chart callbacks. Selected metadata is compared directly rather than rebuilding identity strings on every poll. Expensive loading/editor work still gets separate, per-widget fair slices, and pending input takes priority. Discovery uses numeric telemN sources and custom sensor metadata from model.getSensor , never names or units alone. Supported single-module families are CRSF (including ELRS) and native FrSky S.Port; unknown/MULTI or multiple active modules fall back rather than guessing. CRSF barometric altitude is ID 0x09 /instance 0; GPS position, groundspeed, and satellite count are ID 0x02 /instances 0, 2, and 5. S.Port uses the firmware barometric/GPS position/groundspeed ID ranges, with matching GPS/speed instances. Calculated sensors and GPS altitude are excluded. Ambiguous categories are disabled independently. GPS requires fresh valid coordinates/delay and, on CRSF, at least four fresh satellites. Numeric inputs reject nonfinite values and normalize metres/feet and knots/m/s/ft/s/km/h/mph. Altitude references require an observed disarmed-to-armed transition using a recent sample explicitly witnessed while disarmed, or fresh evidence at that transition. Merely current late readings never rebase an armed session. Motor interruptions preserve the reference but reset holds; unknown arm resets holds without inventing disarm. Metadata changes and scheduling gaps invalidate the reference conservatively. Fixed shortcuts are strictly above +3 m or 10 mph for at least 200 ticks, allowing only precision-scaled conversion roundoff (including float32 firmware). smartStatus explains fallback in the native Model settings dialog; confirmed field changes persist and update live detection immediately. Model settings use their own schema/revision and losslessly encoded model filename under /AEROGRID/models/ . Saves verify model identity and revision before verified file replacement. Layout saves and previews never write this document. Legacy detector declarations remain compatible until model settings are changed; retained arm metadata stays with its layout rather than becoming model-wide Armed. Schema version 1 has an optional top-level armed condition: missing preserves per-consumer legacy fallback, while "" explicitly disables arming, including fallbacks. Nonempty values must be physical positions or logical switches L01–L64 (optionally inverted). Numeric channel IDs are rejected. The model document is loaded in a separate callback before Armed and panel construction. Saving a different arm condition rebuilds every registered dashboard and clears captured homes, preserving layout data and a pinned active flight's completion/cleanup. Previous per-widget Armed selections are never silently promoted; conflicting old selections require an explicit model choice. The optional top-level sessionReset uses the same switch syntax; missing or "" disables it. A shared control poller detects false-to-true transitions independently of flight detection. Activation advances the flight epoch, cancels detection, releases its owned output, and stages every dashboard's reload with captured homes cleared and editor drafts retained. Counting waits for a fresh disarm observation. Model changes also reset the flight epoch; ordinary dashboard rebuilds do not.

docs.text: Use panels/flight-mode.lua as a small working example and lib/panel_host.lua as the authoritative contract. Declaration or callback Role id , apiVersion , supportedSpans Identify the module, check compatibility, and advertise valid grid sizes. settings Typed fields, defaults, bounds, and choices used by validation and the editor. refreshInterval Desired foreground interval in 10 ms ticks; work still shares the host budget. refreshCost Whole-number share of the six host refresh slots (default 1). Chart uses all six so dense layouts cannot batch expensive redraws into one callback. create(parent, rect, settings, services) Build LVGL objects, subscribe to data, and return private instance state. refresh(context) Optional callback to update existing objects from snapshots. May return a whole-number interval of 1–6000 ticks; nil preserves the current interval. A second result of true reserves subsequent turns among panels of the same type until the update completes; other panel types and services continue running. update(context, rect, settings, detailsOnly, placement) Optional geometry/configuration update. Host reflows and editor resizes pass the current grid placement as the fifth argument, leaving the internal detailsOnly argument unset. background(context) Optional work when the dashboard is not visible. event(context, event) Optional event handling; return true when consumed. destroy(context) Optional cleanup of panel-owned references. validateSettings(settings, span, config) Optional cross-field and span-dependent validation. Put the module at panels/<type>.lua and reference that type in a layout. Regular panels declare supportedSpans = { "any" } and adapt their contents to every in-bounds span of the 4 x 4 grid. Use an explicit span list when there is a real rendering constraint: Host diagnostics and Service probe need at least 2x2, Chart needs a wide or square placement at least 2x1, while Theme showcase requires 4x4. Declare only spans you actually render correctly. A list setting ( type = "table" ) declares entry fields with keys or nested paths, labels, types, and appropriate defaults/bounds/choices. The editor uses this schema to offer even fields omitted from the YAML, and can remove cleared optional fields. List declarations, including nested lists, can set itemLabel to a singular name such as "Metric" or "State" . The editor names rows using the first nonempty label or source, then itemLabel and the one-based index; lists without itemLabel use "Entry" . Do not build a separate settings UI for each panel. The public theme.lua API composes palette/state resolution with typography.lua (measurement, font fitting, unit metrics) and panel_layout.lua (frames, slots, bands, and regions). The public primitives.lua API composes LVGL objects with reading.lua (reading/unit composition, redraw detection, and visibility/reflow reconciliation). Installed functions are direct references, not per-call wrappers; each widget has its own caches and mutable API tables. The host supplies these dependencies when executing the modules. Pure-Lua tests use tests/support/module_loader.lua to compose the same APIs without installing firmware globals. Use theme.lua for bands, font fitting, shared colors, and spacing, and primitives.lua for reusable LVGL objects. primitives.reading constructs the matching value/unit arrangement used by the battery and link readouts; optional units and differing initial geometry remain panel-specific. Keep a reading's font stable as its value changes, using the widest expected representation to choose it. When changing settings vocabulary or rendering, inspect sibling panels so the same setting retains the same meaning. Add focused tests, an integration case at every declared span, a simulator review layout when useful, and a panel reference page . If adding screenshot support, add a capture recipe and adapter as described in Project tools .

docs.text: editor.lua owns draft operations; editor_ui.lua and editor_drawer.lua present them; editor_controller.lua coordinates them with the live dashboard. layout_store.lua handles saving, backups, and user-versus-shipped resolution; layout_registry.lua maintains name-to-choice positions. Keep these boundaries intact when changing save behavior. Panel settings drawers, including entry subdrawers, put Label first when declared, preserving the declaration order of all remaining controls. Editing does not overwrite bundled layouts. Save writes to /AEROGRID/layouts/ , and Save As creates a named user layout. The layout registry is initialized at script load, so new names require a restart before appearing in the native Layout picker. Save errors must preserve the draft and report failure. Test persistence through the store/editor suites, not just the visible dialog.

docs.text: EdgeTX limits a widget callback to 20,000 Lua VM instructions . Creation, parsing, panel building, reload, and reflow are staged across callbacks. Services have bounded subscription updates, and panel work is capped and phase-staggered. Do not replace this with one synchronous "simpler" loader. The budget tests require strictly less than 75% of the callback allowance. Avoid object churn and retained callbacks. Shared labels install a persistent font callback; change its backing state through primitives.setFont rather than replacing the callback during refresh/reflow. Replacement retained Lua registry references in EdgeTX 2.12.4. Other firmware details already have helpers and regression coverage: theme.measureText uses lcd.sizeText where available and estimates otherwise; trim sources do not identify their axis, image decode failure is not reported by lvgl.image , and lvgl.arc positions use the center rather than the bounding-box corner. Reuse the existing panel logic, file checks, and primitives.arcBounds instead of introducing alternate assumptions.

docs.text: Check out and build AeroGrid is a Lua widget, not a firmware fork. You do not need to build EdgeTX or connect a radio to get started. The development build assembles an SD-card directory that either simulator can boot; the release build creates the ZIP that users install. Get the code With Git installed, clone the repository and create a branch for your change: git clone https://github.com/thomaskistler/aero-grid.git cd aero-grid git switch -c my-change If you do not have repository write access, fork it on GitHub and clone your fork instead. Run all commands in this guide from the repository root. Prerequisites Install Python 3 with virtual-environment support, Make, and rsync. Python 3.11 is the version used in CI. The Makefile uses a Unix shell and bin/ virtual-environment paths: use macOS, Linux, or WSL for these commands. On Windows, Companion can run natively, but must be pointed at a directory accessible from Windows. Set up the development environment make setup make test make setup creates build/venv/ and installs the pinned lupa dependency. There is no need to activate the environment: Make invokes its Python directly. make test also sets up this environment automatically when needed. Install the validation tools Behavior tests need only the Python environment, but runtime changes also need these tools on PATH : Tool Used for Version guidance edgetx-luac or Lua 5.3 luac Parse source and test Lua in make check . Prefer EdgeTX's compiler when available; otherwise use Lua 5.3 , not a different Lua version. lua-language-server Static diagnostics in make lint . CI uses 3.19.1; install the appropriate binary from LuaLS releases . stylua Format Lua and check formatting. CI pins 2.5.2; use StyLua releases . For example, on Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install git make rsync python3 python3-venv lua5.3 make check LUA_COMPILER=luac5.3 On macOS with Homebrew, the basic dependencies and Lua compiler can be installed with: brew install python rsync lua@5.3 make check LUA_COMPILER="$(brew --prefix lua@5.3)/bin/luac" Install LuaLS and StyLua separately and ensure their executables are on PATH . The VS Code Lua extension is useful in the editor, but does not by itself make the LuaLS command-line binary available to Make. make check searches for edgetx-luac , luac5.3 , then luac . If the last one is a different version, pass LUA_COMPILER explicitly. See Test and debug for the complete validation workflow. Build make build This creates the SD image at build/sdcard/ . To see the dashboard, follow Run and test in simulators . What the build does tests/fixtures/sdcard/ radio, models, registry, and model image + src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/ current widget, panels, libraries, and layouts | v build/sdcard/ disposable simulator SD-card root make build copies the fixture first, then overlays the whole widget package. It removes compiled .luac files and updates Lua source timestamps so EdgeTX recompiles the current sources. There is no transpilation or native compilation of AeroGrid itself. Stop the simulator before rebuilding. The build recreates the image from the baseline, deleting simulator-created models, saved layouts, registry changes, and other files not present in the fixture. Back up experiments outside that directory first. Never point a build at a real SD card or personal model backup. Use a separate image when you want an independent experiment: make build BUILD_DIR=build/experiment Its SD-card root is build/experiment/sdcard/ ; change the simulator path to match. Changing BUILD_DIR also relocates Make-managed environments and output. The screenshot tools have their own fixed output paths, described in Project tools . Build an installable package make release-package This writes AeroGrid-<version>.zip and its .sha256 file to build/release/ , using the version in src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/lib/package.lua . The archive contains runtime Lua, the editor assets, the Default , Empty , Diagnostics , and Palette layouts, and the license. Review layouts, fixture models, simulator state, and bytecode are not included. Use this ZIP, rather than the development SD image, to check the actual installation and upgrade procedure . Publishing a release is a separate maintainer workflow . Build and preview the documentation make docs make docs-serve The first command installs the pinned documentation tools into build/docs-venv/ and strictly builds the site at build/docs/ . The second serves a live-reloading preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000 ; stop it with Ctrl-C. This previews the checkout only. The published site's Documentation version menu offers released versions and main . Markdown lives in docs/ . When adding or renaming a page, update both mkdocs.yml and the explicit sidebar in docs/overrides/toc.html . Base site styling is in docs/stylesheets/aerogrid.css ; the shared Radio Console shell, typography, cards, dialogs, help popovers, notices, and disclosures are in docs/stylesheets/console.css . Their existing ag-radio , ag-release , and ag-install class names are also reused by the browser tools; these styles do not load or require those tools. Checked-in screenshots are used as-is; building the site never launches a simulator. Browser installer assets The USB installer modules live in docs/javascripts/ : radio-storage.mjs owns connections and metadata, radio-installer.mjs handles releases and verified widget replacement, radio-panel.mjs drives the installation UI, and radio-connection-help.mjs adds connection help. The site mirrors published stable releases , not the current source tree. Downloads are verified before replacement and installed files are checked afterward. Only WIDGETS/AeroGrid is replaced; user data, maps, other widgets, settings, and firmware are preserved. There is no backup or rollback. To include those assets in a disposable built-site preview: make docs python3 tools/installer_assets.py --output build/docs/installer python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory build/docs Mirroring needs network access to GitHub; optional GH_TOKEN authentication stays server-side. Test in desktop Chrome or Edge over HTTPS or localhost. Ordinary make docs-serve does not mirror installation assets. Releases without mirrored assets remain unavailable for automatic installation. Stop the preview with Ctrl-C. Never direct asset output or a development build at a radio's SD card. Command reference Command Result make help List supported targets. make setup Install development Python dependencies. make test Check the Python runner, then run every Lua behavior suite with firmware-like string behavior. make test-installer Test the browser installer with Node.js 22 and Python. make check Run behavior tests, then parse source/test Lua. make lint Run LuaLS diagnostics. make format Rewrite source/test Lua using StyLua. make build Reset and assemble the development SD image. make capture-setup Install optional panel screenshot dependencies. make release-package Generate the installation ZIP and checksum. make docs / make docs-serve Build / preview the website. make clean Delete the configured build directory, including environments and simulator state.

docs.text: Issues, changes, and releases You can contribute a reproducible bug report, a focused fix, a panel, or clearer documentation. Start with the checkout instructions for code work; you do not need a working development environment to file an issue. File an issue Search existing issues first. If none describes the problem, choose New issue . There are currently no repository-specific issue templates. For a bug report, include: Detail What to provide Summary A specific title and what failed. Version AeroGrid package version or Git commit; EdgeTX version; radio type and display size. Environment Physical radio, VS Code Dev Kit/WASM, Companion native simulator, or mock test; extension/Companion version and desktop OS when relevant. Reproduction Steps from a clean baseline, selected model/layout/theme, and the smallest layout or settings that reproduce it. Expected / actual What should happen and what actually happens, including exact error text. Evidence Relevant logs, screenshots, failing test output, or a recording. For growth/CPU problems, include duration and observed measurements. Data setup Source names/types/units, link state, switches, timers, and any synthetic inputs needed to reproduce it. Attach a minimal YAML layout rather than an entire personal SD card. Remove unrelated model information, GPS coordinates, and other private data before posting. State whether the issue survives a fresh build/restart; that helps separate a code defect from stale bytecode or saved-layout overrides. For a feature request, describe the developer or pilot problem, an example workflow, and the desired behavior. Mention relevant panel sizes and radio constraints. Discuss large behavioral changes before implementing them. docs.text: Run and test in simulators Both simulators run EdgeTX firmware, but use different builds and interfaces. Use VS Code for a tight edit/run loop and Companion for native firmware UI, radio controls, and screenshot tooling. Record which one you used when reporting a result. Simulator What you need Best use VS Code EdgeTX Dev Kit VS Code and the Dev Kit extension; first launch downloads WASM firmware. Editor-integrated runs, watch mode, controls, synthetic telemetry, and logs. EdgeTX Simulator supplied with Companion EdgeTX Companion 2.12 with the TX16S simulator. Native UI/control checks, telemetry simulation, and debugging without VS Code. Neither proves receiver behavior, native radio memory stability, or support for every color radio. Mock memory regression tests python3 tests/run.py includes repeated layout reload/resize checks for retired page and service-runtime collection, stable LVGL object counts, retained Lua memory, and font callback references. The review-output layout participates. A dedicated output-panel test warms all 32 channel rows, then measures 100 cycles of changing outputs/trims, loss/recovery, name and trim ambiguity, channel-range changes, display toggles, and narrow/wide reflows. It requires retained growth below 1 KiB and second-half growth below 0.25 KiB, with no live-object growth. These mock checks catch regressions; they do not replace native-radio soak tests. Prepare a disposable SD image make build Use the absolute path to build/sdcard/ , not src/ , WIDGETS/ , or tests/fixtures/sdcard/ , as the simulator SD-card root. It contains RADIO/ , MODELS/ , IMAGES/ , AEROGRID/ , and WIDGETS/ . Run pwd at the repository root to find the checkout's absolute path. Do not run both simulators against the same image at the same time. They can write files on the simulated SD card. Stop the simulator before rebuilding, back up experiments elsewhere, and remember that make build resets them. Use make build BUILD_DIR=build/companion and point Companion at build/companion/sdcard/ if you want separate state. VS Code: EdgeTX Dev Kit Install EdgeTX Dev Kit ( jeffreychix.edgetx-dev-kit ) from VS Code's Extensions view. The steps here use the extension's 2.x simulator commands; Companion is not required. Open the repository folder in VS Code. Open src/WIDGETS/AeroGrid/main.lua . In the Command Palette, run EdgeTX: Toggle EdgeTX Mode if it is not already active. Confirm the profile is tx16s , 2.12 , color , 480 x 272 , as recorded in .vscode/edgetx.json . If the profile is missing or stale, run EdgeTX: Set Radio Profile . In workspace settings, set EdgeTX: SD Card Path ( edgetx.sdCardPath ) to the absolute generated image path. Run Tasks: Run Task > AeroGrid: Build Simulator SD , or make build in a terminal. The other supplied task, AeroGrid: Test , runs make test . Run EdgeTX: Open Simulator to boot the fixture and inspect its configured models/screens. Allow the initial firmware download to finish. Use Show Controls for switches, sticks, trims, and radio buttons. To launch the active entry point directly, use EdgeTX: Simulate Script . main.lua includes the App-mode simulation annotation ---@simulate Layout1x1AM zone=0 . For the fixture's existing model/screen configuration, prefer Open Simulator rather than relying on script auto-placement. Companion: native EdgeTX Simulator Install EdgeTX Companion 2.12 for your OS, including the TX16S simulator. There are two launch paths: Companion's embedded simulator, available on macOS too, and the standalone EdgeTX Simulator distributed on Windows/Linux. Launch from Companion Open Companion and create/select a radio profile for RadioMaster TX16S . In Edit Settings... , set that profile's SD Structure path to the absolute generated build/sdcard/ directory. Choose File > Read Models and Settings from SD Path . This opens the fixture's radio settings and models in a Companion document without a connected radio. Confirm that the AeroGrid fixture models are present. Use the document's Simulate Radio action ( Alt+Shift+S ) to boot the complete radio. Use Simulate Model ( Alt+S ) if you intentionally want only the selected model. The embedded simulator uses the profile's SD path for widget/layout/image files, but a temporary copy of the document's radio/model data. Do not expect model changes made during this simulation to be written back to the fixture or Companion document. AeroGrid's user layouts are separate SD-card files; treat that SD path as writable. After rebuilding the image, close the simulation and read models/settings from SD Path again before simulating, so an older open document cannot reintroduce stale model configuration. Launch the standalone simulator On Windows/Linux, open the EdgeTX Simulator installed with Companion ( simulator.exe on Windows; packaged executable naming can vary on Linux). Create the TX16S radio profile in Companion first, then configure the standalone simulator's Startup Options : Option Value Radio Profile Your TX16S profile. Radio Type RadioMaster TX16S. Simulator The available TX16S simulator matching that profile. Data Source SD Path . SD Image Path The absolute path to the generated build/sdcard/ . Click OK . SD Path makes the simulator load radio/model data from the same image that contains the widget. Do not select a default/new .etx data file: that boots a different model configuration. If using Folder instead, set Data Folder and SD Image Path to that same SD-card root, not its MODELS/ subdirectory. The image contains RADIO/radio.yml and MODELS/model*.yml ; the standalone simulator loads these directly and persists radio/model changes. You do not need to import them individually or read a connected radio. If no simulator is listed, check the installed Companion package and profile before modifying the fixture. Use the fixture models A clean build selects AG Overview , with Default on its first screen. Change models with the simulated radio's model-selection UI, just as on a radio. Model What to exercise AG Overview ( model1.yml ) Default; sim; sim2. AG Flight ( model2.yml ) review-model-identity; review-flight-mode; review-flight-timer; review-flight-counter; review-chart. AG Power-Link ( model3.yml ) review-rx-battery; review-cell-sources; review-tx-battery; review-link-status; review-metric. AG Navigation ( model4.yml ) review-navigation. AG Controls ( model5.yml ) review-output; review-trim-panel. AG System ( model6.yml ) Diagnostics; services; services2; review-state; states; Palette; Empty. Review and simulator-only layouts live in tests/fixtures/layouts/development/ ; make build adds them to the disposable simulator image without including them in the widget source or release ZIP. Together the categories expose all 23 registered layouts exactly once, in the screen order shown above. Layout filenames and registry indices are unchanged. All six models share the same sensors, physical switches, mixes, trims, and timer setup. EdgeTX stores each model's live timer and trim state separately. AG Flight also reserves Sticky L01 for AeroGrid's flight-status output. Its Special Functions play three Beep 1 tones when L01 turns on and four when it turns off, using the supplied one-shot agstart and agend audio tracks. They do not play at model startup. All screens use App mode and the Modern Dark theme. On the State dashboard, SF changes MODE, SA changes RATE, and SB changes FLAP; NO MIDDLE deliberately leaves SA's middle position unmapped. The sixth screen of AG System is the telemetry-free Palette layout. Its fixed samples show token swatches, text levels, accents, a dial, bars, and the six dashboard panel states. Change the widget's Theme option to compare Modern Dark and Modern Light, or add a .yml theme file as described in Customize themes . Diagnostics reports loading, package identity, and service errors; services and services2 exercise the service-probe panel across all five services. sim and sim2 are complementary live-data dashboards: the first focuses on telemetry, while the second focuses on radio-local values and metric modes. Development layouts are not included in the release ZIP. AG Flight uses SF down for model-wide arming, ten-second start and end detection windows, and Smart detection enabled. Raise CH3 above 25% and supply live telemetry to exercise flight detection. Its flight-counter screen displays the shared model count; resize it in the editor to inspect other spans. Rebuild and re-import models/settings into Companion to replace the former STD/PANEL1/PANEL2 models. Existing Companion documents retain their old screens until refreshed; make build replaces the generated simulator image.

docs.text: Test and debug Use the quickest test that exercises your change while iterating, then run the broader checks before submitting. Mock tests validate logic; simulators validate the actual firmware UI; a radio validates hardware behavior. None substitutes for all the others. Run the automated Lua suites make test make check make test checks the Python test runner, then executes every test_*.lua beneath tests/ , excluding support modules. Each Lua suite gets a fresh lupa.lua53.LuaRuntime and the repository root as its chunk argument. The runner captures console lines beginning with [AeroGrid] ERROR so expected negative cases do not clutter successful runs. Other output, including progress and performance measurements, remains visible. If a suite fails, its captured logs and file path are printed to stderr before the original traceback, and the run stops with a non-zero exit status. Logs from earlier passing suites are discarded. This affects only tests/run.py ; production logging is unchanged. Tests that replace print themselves still own the output they intercept. Every suite runs once with the string metatable removed to resemble EdgeTX. Runtime code should use string.sub(value, ...) , not assume value:sub(...) works on the radio. make check runs those same tests and then parses all source/test Lua with the detected compiler. The runner explicitly selects Lua 5.3 to match EdgeTX, rather than lupa 's default runtime, which can change between releases. Mock behavior tests still do not replace firmware compiler validation. Install the compiler , or specify it: make check LUA_COMPILER=/absolute/path/to/edgetx-luac Choose the right test layer Change Start here YAML, layout validation, geometry, or persistence tests/unit/lib/ and tests/support/assertions.lua . Source resolution, freshness, model/control/navigation data The corresponding service suite in tests/unit/lib/ . Panel settings or presentation tests/unit/panels/ , then the relevant tests/integration/widget/test_*_review.lua . Host load/reload, failure isolation, scheduling, or callback budgets tests/integration/test_widget.lua . Editor commands and settings dialogs tests/unit/lib/test_editor.lua and tests/integration/test_editor_ui.lua . docs.text: Project tools These tools exist to make AeroGrid development reproducible. They do not run on the radio, and their generated output belongs in ignored build/ directories unless you deliberately publish reviewed documentation assets. For native walkthrough recording, cached Cora narration, and radio-photo compositing, see Tutorial videos . Capture documentation images with native firmware The capture tools load Companion's native TX16S simulator library directly through tools/capture-native.cpp . They create isolated SD images and widget copies; they do not modify src/ or your active build/sdcard/ . VS Code is not involved. Requirements are macOS , EdgeTX Companion 2.12, and Xcode command-line tools ( clang++ and lipo ). The tools require a single-architecture TX16S simulator library; an Intel library on Apple Silicon needs Rosetta. The default application path is /Applications/EdgeTX Companion 2.12.app ; pass --companion "/path/to/Companion.app" to choose another installation. These tools are local-only and do not run in CI. Panel screenshots make capture-setup build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-panels.py --panel trim-panel build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-panels.py --all Choose one of --panel <type> , --recipe <path> , or --all . make capture-setup installs pinned PyYAML in a separate environment. All thirteen user-facing panel types, plus the Host diagnostics and Service probe utility panels, have bundled recipes. Each panel writes to build/doc-capture/<panel>/ : Output Purpose 1x2.png , 2x1.png , 2x2.png Gallery crops with recipe-defined borders. full-frame.png , frame.rgb565 Full display and raw framebuffer for inspection. recipe.yaml , provenance.json Exact inputs, geometry, source/tool hashes, simulator digest, and disclosures. sdcard/ , simulator.log Isolated fixture and diagnostics. Regenerating a panel replaces its previous output directory ; there is no run history. --all runs recipes sequentially, so a failure leaves earlier successful panels updated. A failed run keeps diagnostics, raises an error, and does not publish documentation assets. Default panel captures use a 480 x 272 Modern Dark/App-mode dashboard with placements outside the menu overlay. Crops are unscaled; a 10-pixel border gives output dimensions of 137 x 154, 258 x 85, and 258 x 154 respectively. Recipes can override the border. Chart omits the unsupported 1x2 placement. Its adapter generates varying synthetic readings through the real telemetry/history services, records for two flights separated by a recording pause, and waits for confirmed completion and finished projection before capturing. This shows neutral flight bands, arm/disarm triangles, and a resume gap with dotted connectors. Its recipe requires armSwitch: SFv ; the adapter supplies that condition and a motor channel through the real services, with isolated model flight settings. The runner waits for recipe-specific readiness, not just a fixed delay. Timer, trim, flight-mode, and model-image samples use isolated firmware model settings. Other recipes use capture-only firmware API inputs passed through the real services and panels . They demonstrate actual EdgeTX rendering, not the correctness of a receiver's telemetry. Change a capture recipe Recipes live in tools/capture-recipes/*.yaml . Copy an existing recipe to an untracked experiment location and select it explicitly: build/capture-venv/bin/python tools/capture-panels.py --recipe /path/to/example.yaml The recipe specifies panel , theme , border , named panels placements, each placement's config , and sample inputs. Positions are zero-based in the 4 x 4 grid and must not overlap. Row spans are currently limited to 1 or 2; span-shaped image names must match the placement's dimensions. Validation runs before startup, then the widget validates panel settings. Use the bundled recipe for the exact sample schema. Examples include timer name/start/remaining seconds, signed stored trim values, TX voltage, and sample.sources with exact sensor names, values, EdgeTX units, and precision. Cells use a voltage list; GPS uses coordinates including pilot position. Every configured source needs a sample. tools/capture_recipes.py owns recipe validation, model setup, synthetic inputs, and readiness adapters. capture-panels.py handles preparation, native invocation, cropping, borders, and provenance. Add an adapter, not production panel logic, when a new sample type needs capture support. Be explicit about capture-only differences: brighten_supporting_text: true uses the resolved muted color for faint text ( #C4CDD3 to #DCE2E6 in Modern Dark) for computer readability; omit it or set false for production colors. The timer's hide_bottom_bar: true hides its bar without reflow. It is not a supported production setting. Metric/link-status examples can omit visuals through config.visual: none . This is a production setting, not evidence that all presentations were tested. The flight-counter gallery panels share one detector and reach their sample count through one real GV9 FM0 increment in the isolated model. Model images resolve relative to the recipe and need a firmware-safe PNG name. Establish redistribution permission before publishing a replacement image; the bundled Crack Yak image's permission was confirmed by its contributor. Capture instrumentation follows the runtime module boundaries: panel captures inject synthetic service inputs and optional text-color overrides into the isolated lib/dashboard_loader.lua ; editor captures call context.editorController.openEditor . Readiness checks wrap the isolated main.lua refresh export. Update these hooks when moving runtime code; do not add capture-specific behavior to production modules. Run the capture-recipe tests after changing recipes/adapters, then inspect the resulting frame and provenance. Editor and setup screenshots python3 tools/capture-editor.py python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene select-layout python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene navigation-location python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene chart-settings python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene chart-metric-entry The navigation-location scene enters fullscreen and taps the navigation panel using native touch input. It closes and reopens the location overlay twice before capturing the frozen Google Maps QR code. This tool uses the same native capture runner; panel-drawer scenes also need PyYAML from make capture-setup . It covers setup/widget/layout choices, editor overview, Metric/State settings, entry dialogs, exit, and Save As. Every other panel has a <panel>-settings scene (for example --scene flight-timer-settings ) that captures its full settings drawer from the panel's capture recipe config, for the panel reference pages. Use --help for supported scene names. Panel drawer scenes save SFv as the model-wide Arm switch, so obsolete panel arm controls are not shown. The Chart scenes use a native GV1 source labeled Reading . chart-settings selects rolling to include Window duration ; chart-metric-entry opens Chart's own entry drawer, not Metric's. The aero-menu , model-settings , model-settings-reset , and model-settings-bottom scenes show the shared model menu and settings. It also captures the telemetry-free Palette layout with real production primitives. These scenes are opt-in and do not open the editor: python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene theme-modern-dark python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene theme-modern-light python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene theme-custom The custom scene uses a fixed blue-gray palette with warm text and green default accents. To experiment interactively, add a .yml file in the user theme directory described in Customize themes . Panel recipes also accept theme: modern-light for checking individual instruments in the built-in light palette. Each selected scene writes a PNG, isolated SD card, framebuffer, and log under build/editor-capture/<scene>/ . The root provenance.json records the selected scenes and source/simulator hashes. Selected scene directories are replaced on regeneration, and the root provenance describes the current invocation, not a merged history of earlier runs. Setup scenes automate native touch input. Editor scenes enter fullscreen through a native long-press and automate production editor commands in the isolated copy. Check images manually: capture success is not a replacement for interactive editor/persistence tests. The settings , <kind>-settings , state-entry , state-condition , metric-entry , and chart-metric-entry scenes capture the whole configuration drawer, cropped to the dialog. When its rows do not fit on the screen, the tool captures further pages in <scene>-page<N>/ , each hiding leading rows in the isolated copy so later rows move into view, and stitches them into one taller PNG. Hidden rows are used instead of scrolling because the native dialog keeps its focused row in view. The scrollbar is painted over, since it reflects only one page. Full dashboard screenshot python3 tools/capture-editor.py --scene dashboard This opt-in scene captures the entire 480 x 272 display, not a composition of panel crops. It uses the shipped Default layout and Modern Dark theme without color or presentation overrides, entering fullscreen through native touch input without opening the editor. The isolated model uses the permitted bundled Crack Yak image, a stopped timer at 5:47 of 10:00, GV9 flight count 42, and GV1 expo 30. Capture-only firmware API inputs supply telemetry, transmitter voltage, and a disarmed SF switch through the real services. Readiness checks verify all nine panels and their primary readings before the native runner waits for the full frame to stabilize. These are illustrative readings, not live receiver telemetry. The PNG and diagnostics are in build/editor-capture/dashboard/ ; the root provenance.json also records the sample inputs, bitmap digest, capture tool hashes, and unmodified production source hashes. Publish reviewed images Panel reference images live in docs/assets/panels/<panel>/ . After reviewing the full frame, crops, and provenance, copy only the intended gallery PNGs and matching provenance.json there. Update the reference-page captions if samples, synthetic inputs, or presentation overrides changed. Editor images live in docs/assets/editor/ . Copy the selected PNGs and the corresponding provenance, taking care not to describe images from several runs with a provenance file for only one scene. The reviewed full-dashboard image and its corresponding provenance live in docs/assets/dashboard/ . The README and website home page share this PNG. Keep SD images, raw framebuffers, logs, and incidental full frames in ignored output. Run make docs after publishing assets. Website builds use the checked-in images and need neither Companion nor capture dependencies. Package a release deterministically make release-package python3 tools/package-release.py --version-only python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_release_*.py' tools/package-release.py reads the package version, checks required layouts/assets, rejects unexpected runtime files and symlinks, and writes a deterministic source-only ZIP plus SHA-256 checksum. Its explicit allowlists include Default , Empty , Diagnostics , and Palette , excluding review layouts and mutable simulator data. Use --output <directory> to choose another output location. See Issues, changes, and releases for publishing; making a local ZIP does not tag or upload anything.
