docs.text: Record and recreate tutorial videos tools/video.py provides reusable local native TX16S recording, Microsoft Cora narration, and FFmpeg compositing. It does not upload to YouTube. Recipes and real input scripts are versioned in tools/video-recipes/ . Generated SD cards, recordings, caches, and provenance belong in ignored build/video/ . No product photograph, credentials, or video is distributed with the repository. Install and run Use Python 3.9+ and make video-setup to install pinned imageio-ffmpeg==0.6.0 (including its encoder) into build/video-venv . Capture additionally requires macOS, Xcode command-line tools, and EdgeTX Companion 2.12. The default simulator library is: /Applications/EdgeTX Companion 2.12.app/Contents/Resources/libedgetx-tx16s-simulator.dylib Override with --library /path/to/libedgetx-tx16s-simulator.dylib . Compilation selects the library's architecture; for a universal library use --architecture arm64 or --architecture x86_64 . Running Intel firmware on Apple Silicon requires Rosetta. The symbol ABI and geometry are TX16S-specific. Rendering and speech caching do not require Companion. make video-setup build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py --help build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py validate build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py capture The default recipe is add-move-resize-panel.json . Select the other tutorial with --recipe tools/video-recipes/create-empty-dashboard.json on each command. --output build/video/my-run selects a different working directory. compile only builds the recorder; prepare only creates an SD card. capture does both, then records. Preparation refuses an existing SD card: use a new output directory for another capture. It never replaces your development SD image. Capture uses capture-editor.py 's SD preparation and the current checkout's widget source, including uncommitted changes. All editor interactions go through genuine simulator touch/key input. No panel code is rewritten. The editing recipe explicitly injects demonstration telemetry only in its isolated widget copy : registered GSpd /maximum sensor, values 48/72, RSSI 85. Those values demonstrate the UI, not receiver telemetry accuracy. Narration without storing credentials speech is offline by default . Cache files are addressed by SHA-256 of text, voice, rate, and PCM format. Text/rate changes require new speech; timing changes reuse a clip if it still fits. Each WAV must be 48 kHz, 16-bit mono PCM, nonempty, intact, and at least 0.3 seconds shorter than its slot. Oversized clips fail rather than silently speeding up or truncating the voice. Increase a recipe's rate percentage or shorten text and retry. Paid synthesis requires an explicit opt-in: # Set AZURE_SPEECH_KEY securely in your terminal/environment, not in a file, # command argument, recipe, shell history, or checked-in configuration. export AZURE_SPEECH_REGION=westus2 build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py speech --online unset AZURE_SPEECH_KEY AZURE_SPEECH_REGION The REST request uses en-US-CoraMultilingualNeural ; existing clips are not resynthesized. The tool never writes keys or logs request headers. Synthesis can incur Azure charges and sends narration text to Azure. A failed later clip leaves previously successful cache entries for retry. To reuse privately retained prototype clips without synthesis: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py speech --cache-source /path/to/private/clips This trusts recipe legacy_cache filenames as matching the text. WAV format and duration are checked, but spoken content and synthesis rate cannot be inferred from audio: listen before importing. Import provenance records this uncertainty. No imported media is required or included. --cache selects an alternate cache directory; keep it ignored. Render and inspect # Screen-only preview, no network or speech needed: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py render --silent --limit 12 # Final photo composite with previously cached narration: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py render --photo /path/to/private/tx16s-upscaled.webp # Render a retained raw recording instead of capturing again: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py render --raw /path/to/recording.rgb565 \ --photo /path/to/private/tx16s-upscaled.webp render never synthesizes speech. Omit --photo for a 480×272 screen-only video (physical button feedback is then omitted). --silent bypasses all speech cache requirements. --limit renders an initial excerpt, not a new capture. Re-rendering replaces outputs in that directory. The supplied photograph must match the recipe geometry. Original source: RadioMaster TX16S product photograph . The original retrieved image was 1000×1000; the prototypes used a user-supplied 4000×4000 upscale . The tool does not download or upscale it. Confirm usage rights and retain attribution to RadioMaster when publishing; the repository's GPL does not license that photograph. For that upscale, recipes crop [width,height,x,y] = [2080,1000,960,2700] , scale to 1560×750, place the 930×532 simulator screen at (317,80), and place RTN feedback at (147,507). The generated bezel mask keeps dark irregular screen edges: inside the screen rectangle, average RGB brightness 80–120 ramps from opaque photo to transparent opening. Inspect the result; a different photo requires different geometry/thresholds. Feedback is a 15%-opacity ring with transparent interior, expanding and fading over 1.2 seconds. Its color adapts to the local framebuffer luminance; drag contacts follow their scripted points. RTN uses a white ring on the dark physical key; other keys have no invented photo coordinates. No titles or subtitle track are burned in. Outputs include: File Purpose frames.rgb565 , last-frame.png , simulator.log Recorder evidence and diagnostics. frame-*.png , frames-sheet.png Frames exported by the frames command for review. sdcard/ , video-native Isolated firmware fixture and compiled recorder. feedback.mov , radio.png , bezel.png Regenerable render intermediates. <recipe-id>.mp4 , transcript.txt H.264/AAC deliverable and narration text. capture-provenance.json , render-provenance.json Recipe, source/input digests, disclosures, tail holds, verification limits. Capture fails if any touch press in the rendered timeline (after warmup and trim_start ) has no matching firmware TE_PRESSED entry in simulator.log , and records unaccepted_touch_ticks in capture provenance. This catches dropped input, not wrong navigation. Export frames to check key states: build/video-venv/bin/python tools/video.py frames --times 0,7.3,21.3,42.1,54.65 --times uses rendered-timeline seconds. PNGs and a tiled frames-sheet.png are written to the output directory. Raw capture is RGB565 little-endian, 480×272, 20 fps. The recorder uses 10 ms ticks, drops the warmup interval, and samples every five ticks. Rendering trims trim_start seconds from that recording and holds the final frame if narration extends past it; the hold duration is recorded. Capture hashes all current widget sources, not just the Git revision. External recordings have no automatically reconstructed capture provenance. FFmpeg decoding and frame counts prove media integrity, not UI success . Review the whole video for correct navigation, drag, save behavior, voice alignment, source units, and photo placement before publishing. Recipe format and reproducibility Version 1 is validated before execution; unknown fields are rejected. Recipes require id , initial ( fresh-model or empty-dashboard ), ticks , warmup_ticks , trim_start , duration , recipe-relative actions , narration , radio , and provenance . Optional sample_telemetry: true is supported only for the editing fixture. Tick totals/warmup are multiples of five. Action rows contain tick x y down ; down is 1 or 0. Negative x encodes key -x-1 ( -2 is RTN). Consecutive touch-down positions are a drag, terminated by a release. Contacts cannot overlap. Narration entries have ordered, nonoverlapping start / end seconds, text , and nonnegative rate (percentage); legacy_cache is optional. Radio entries contain crop , even-sized canvas , [x,y,width,height] screen , [x,y] return_button , [low,high] mask_threshold , and source . Provenance requires status and notes . Create Empty dashboard: a clean native replay starting from a fresh model with no configured screens. It replaces the default screen with an App-mode AeroGrid widget using the Empty layout (tapped at (220,85)) and Modern Dark, then presses RTN three times. No recorded frames are edited. The firmware dropped the first scripted touch of a fresh simulator session in earlier attempts, desynchronizing every later step. The action script therefore primes input before recorded frames start: a center tap opens the EdgeTX menu and RTN closes it (ticks 100–220), so the video begins on the unchanged main view. Two consecutive Companion 2.12 captures were visually verified before rendering the published 54.7-second video. Add/move/resize panel: the recipe preserves the prototype's real touch script, current/maximum speed configuration, movement, resizing, and save interaction. Nine seconds are trimmed from the raw capture, including most of its first long-press; check intro timing. The last second is a held frame. Radio restart and selecting the new layout after Save as are narrated instructions , not automated or demonstrated steps. Panel unit appearance comes from production source, never simulator-only rendering patches. Fixed-coordinate/realtime scripts can change behavior with firmware, machine load, or widget changes. There is no UI-state assertion or automatic recovery. Keep the approved published videos separately; recipes are maintainable starting points, not a guarantee of identical recreation. Validate changes build/video-venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_video.py Tests cover recipe/action validation, isolated source preservation, cache behavior, request escaping via a mocked Azure response, and offline screen/photo render-and-decode smoke checks. Real native capture is local and must be checked separately. Never require paid speech in tests.

docs.text: Chart 2x1 2x2 Records up to three numeric EdgeTX sources on one chart while armed or in flight. The legend shows each recorded value and its minimum and maximum. Wide layouts keep the legend on the right. Square and tall layouts put it above the full-width plot, with two or three metrics arranged left to right. Use separate panels for separate charts. Select Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings ; changes save automatically. Until model arming has been saved, an existing panel arm switch remains in use and visible. Saved model arming overrides it on every dashboard; saved None disables recording rather than restoring the fallback. Settings Setting Default What it does Label empty Optional chart heading. Clear it to hide the heading. Metrics none Up to three readings. Tap + to add one, or tap an entry to edit it. Time range growing growing keeps the recording from the start; rolling shows the latest fixed window. Window duration 1 minute 30 seconds , 1 minute , 2 minutes , 5 minutes , or 10 minutes . Shown only when Time range is rolling . Series scales shared shared uses one vertical scale; independent gives each metric its own scale, useful for unlike units. Independent trace heights are not directly comparable. Line smoothing off off , light , medium , or strong . Smooths the line only, not the recorded value or extrema. Accent cyan Panel stripe color: cyan , green , amber , or orange . Does not change trace colors. Metric entry Tap a reading under Metrics to open its settings. Setting Default What it does Label source name Name in the legend. Clear it to use the source name. Source required Numeric EdgeTX source to record. Range min , Range max Auto Optional lower and upper vertical bounds, in steps of 0.1. Step below the lowest numeric value to select Auto . If both are set, maximum must exceed minimum. Unit sensor unit Unit text beside the value. Changes the label, not the number. Precision Sensor Decimal places, 0 to 3. Step below 0 to select Sensor , using the source's precision. Color by entry order Trace and legend color: cyan , green , orange , or amber . Defaults to cyan, orange, then green; cyan uses blue ink in Modern Light. An explicit choice keeps that color. Remove entry Deletes this reading. Behavior Recording starts when the effective armed condition is active. When shared flight detection uses that same condition, recording continues through the disarm grace until flight end is confirmed, even while the chart is hidden. Rearming during grace keeps one uninterrupted flight. Without a qualified, matching flight, disarming pauses recording immediately. A neutral background band identifies each flight behind the grid and telemetry traces: lighter in dark themes, darker in light themes. Its edges use the actual flight times, not the later qualification or confirmation times; an active flight's band grows with the recording. Grace-period samples remain on the chart beyond the band's end. No Flight counter panel or logical-switch output is required. A chart opened mid-flight shades only the recorded portion. Upward triangles on the bottom axis mark arming; downward triangles mark disarming. The first arming that starts recording is not marked. Pausing simply stops the traces, without a label or stop marker. Resuming inserts a gap; dotted lines connect the last recorded values to the resumed values. The gap indicates omitted time, not the length of the pause. Missing telemetry breaks the traces without adding a pause gap or connector. Readouts freeze when recording pauses. Minimum and maximum cover all recorded periods, even in rolling mode. Growing starts at one minute and expands in whole-minute steps as cumulative recording time increases. Rolling drops plot history outside Window duration , but keeps the recorded minimum and maximum. Faint solid grid lines mark recording-time intervals; the bottom-right label shows the recording-time window. Very dense pause gaps can push older points out of view. Each vertical bound can be fixed independently: set only Range min to anchor the bottom, only Range max to fix the top, or both for a fixed range. Auto follows recorded extrema with some padding. With shared scales, the lowest configured minimum and highest configured maximum apply to all traces; an unset side follows all metrics automatically. With independent scales, each metric uses its own bounds. Fixed bounds clip the plot, not recorded values or extrema. Smoothing reduces short-term fluctuations in the line. docs.text: Flight counter 1x2 2x1 2x2 Displays the model's GV9 flight total and highlights a detected active flight. Flight tracking is shared by AeroGrid dashboards and does not require a visible Flight counter. Settings Setting Default What it does Label FLT Panel heading. Clear it to restore the default. Select Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings . Changes apply immediately to every dashboard for the model. Until model arming is set, retained legacy Flight counter arm conditions remain in use and must agree for shared flight tracking. Conflicts require an explicit model selection, not an automatic choice. Saving None disables arming, including legacy fallbacks. Model flight settings Configure motor output, start/end detection windows, Smart detection, Session reset switch, and Flight status switch in Model settings . These settings save automatically and apply to the model's dashboards, including Empty dashboards. The panel drawer only configures its label. Existing layouts keep their detection settings until you change Model settings. If older counters disagree, choose the intended configuration explicitly. Configure Model settings before removing the last legacy counter. Behavior A flight qualifies when the effective armed condition, Motor threshold (%) , and live telemetry hold continuously for the Start detection window . Any interruption before qualification resets the attempt. Qualification increments the total once. Motor percentage maps the channel's normal low-to-high travel to 0–100%, after applying Reverse motor . With Smart detection on, a flight can also qualify when trustworthy barometric altitude is more than 3 metres above its arming reference for 2 continuous seconds , or valid GPS groundspeed is more than 10 mph for 2 continuous seconds . Both shortcuts still require armed state, motor above the configured threshold, and live telemetry. The fixed speed rule is a provisional heuristic, not a guaranteed taxi/flight discriminator. Smart discovers supported CRSF/ELRS and FrSky S.Port sensors automatically. Open Model settings to see sensor readiness or why standard detection is being used. Missing, ambiguous, stale, or unsupported sensors never block standard qualification. Altitude needs a trustworthy recent reading seen while disarmed or freshly received at the observed arm transition; starting AeroGrid already armed or receiving altitude late does not establish that reference. Healthy half-second and one-second updates are supported. Current means Smart is bridging a normal interval between updates; stopped or unverifiable streams fall back to standard detection. Low flights and short hops are not guaranteed to qualify early. The model's Arm switch overrides panel arm switches and also drives Chart, first-arm Navigation, and flight-session minima in this widget. Custom State-panel conditions remain independent. An unavailable arm reading cannot confirm disarming. After qualification, telemetry or motor changes do not end the flight. Continuous disarming starts the End detection window (s) . Re-arming before it expires cancels the pending end without counting again. A callback gap of more than one second restarts qualification or a pending end timeout rather than assuming the condition held while unobserved. Tracking continues through hidden dashboards, layout/theme rebuilds, and panel previews while AeroGrid callbacks are running. Adding counters does not create another detector. Reserve GV9 in flight mode 0, with precision 0 and limits allowing 0–999. The existing total is kept, including one previously written by EdgeTX Flights. Invalid or unsavable counts produce an error rather than wrapping. Do not also run EdgeTX Flights or another GV9 flight counter. Configure other flight modes to inherit GV9 from flight mode 0. If dashboard arm conditions conflict or settings change during a flight, the current flight finishes using its original condition and output. New flights wait until the configuration is consistent. Optional logical-switch output First configure a dedicated Sticky logical switch in EdgeTX, with no inputs, AND condition, delay, or duration. Then select it in Flight status switch . The list shows configured logical switches plus None . The output must not also be the flight's Arm or Session reset input. AeroGrid changes only its state, not its model configuration. Use the switch in your own Special Functions or sounds. The output turns true at qualification and false after confirmed completion, including the disarm grace period. A full command buffer is reported and retried. Do not share this output with another script. It is not a safety interlock: stopped Lua execution, model changes, or transmitter restarts cannot guarantee output cleanup. The Session reset switch cancels detection and clears its output without changing GV9. Disarm before another flight can be counted. AeroGrid does not write flight CSV files. GV9 persists through model saving and transmitter restarts, but in-flight detection state does not. Changing model or restarting during a flight can lose its history and qualify it again. States Condition Presentation Resting or qualifying Count and normal styling, without a badge. Qualified flight or pending disarm timeout Count, mist blue surface, blue accent, and IN-FLIGHT badge. If the blue surface would be illegible, the surface keeps its normal color. Confirmed completion Count retained and normal styling restored. GV9 unavailable -- and an N/A badge. Configuration or persistence failure Actionable service error; resolve it before relying on tracking.

docs.text: Host diagnostics Displays facts read from the running AeroGrid host: loaded files, theme, panel failures, source bindings, or a shared event log. This diagnostic panel is for developers and users investigating a dashboard that behaves unexpectedly, rather than for monitoring a flight. The panel needs at least 2x2 cells to fit its rows. Settings Setting Default What it does Label section name Panel heading. Clear it to use the selected Section . Section identity Report to show: identity , theme , panels , sources , or log . Maximum log entries 64 Shown for log . Retains 1–256 messages radio-wide. When several log panels exist, the largest requested limit applies. Accent cyan Panel accent: cyan , green , amber , or orange . Diagnostic messages do not change the panel color. Remove panel Deletes the panel from the screen. Behavior identity reports the package version, main script size and modification time when available, whether compiled bytecode is present, the layout selection and resolved path, and the model filename. RUNNING main.luac warns that EdgeTX can prefer the compiled file over the source; the source timestamp alone does not prove which code is executing. theme reports the resolved theme, where its selection came from, any fallback from a requested theme, and host notices. panels reports the panel count, failure count, and each panel's identifier, type, and span. Rejected and failed panels appear before healthy ones, with their error text. sources reports the shared telemetry subscriptions: the requested source names, binding identifiers and states. Unbound sources appear first. An unbound name may be misspelled or absent on the radio; the report cannot distinguish the two. Reports read the live host context rather than resolving the layout or theme again. Lines are left-aligned and refresh about twice per second. The panel shows only the lines that fit, up to twelve; enlarge it to reveal more. Long reports can still extend beyond that limit. Shared log Select log on at least one Host diagnostics panel before reproducing a problem. Recording is enabled only while a live log panel exists on any AeroGrid screen; it need not be the visible screen. Other sections and editor previews do not enable recording. Background callbacks keep Navigation running on hidden screens. The in-memory buffer is shared by all AeroGrid widget instances. Each entry contains uptime ( hh:mm:ss ), originating layout and runtime host number ( layout#host ), panel ID, and message. The host number distinguishes two instances using the same layout; it is not an EdgeTX screen number. Navigation currently records first-arm captured/missed outcomes and switch availability failures, along with raw decision inputs: current tick, availability/freshness/stale state/value/update tick, delay in seconds, and coordinate validity (not coordinates). Inputs describe GPS for capture attempts, or the arm switch for switch-unavailable events. Missing values appear as nil . It does not log every refresh, retry capture, or change the one-second capture policy. The dashboard shows the newest messages that fit, clipped to one row each. History shifts repaint newest rows first in small batches. Enter widget fullscreen, then tap the log panel to open a full-height viewer. Drag down or turn the scroll wheel left for older lines; drag up or turn right for newer lines. Long messages wrap. The viewer opens at the newest messages and freezes a snapshot so new events cannot move text while it is being read. Close and reopen to see newer events. Close or RTN returns to the dashboard. Touch is unavailable outside widget fullscreen in EdgeTX. Oldest entries are evicted at the configured limit. Removing the panel with the largest limit trims history to the remaining panels' limit on the next read or event. Removing all log panels stops recording but keeps existing history in memory. Nothing is written to the SD card; restarting the radio or unloading the widget script loses the log. docs.text: Navigation 1x2 2x1 2x2 Shows distance from home and the north-up bearing from home toward the model, with optional GPS coordinates and satellite count. Bearing is not aircraft heading, transmitter orientation, or a return-home instruction. Settings Setting Default What it does Label NAV Panel heading. GPS source GPS EdgeTX GPS source supplying the model's coordinates. It must return a coordinate table. Home position edgetx edgetx uses EdgeTX home; first-arm captures home using the effective armed condition. Satellite count source none Optional source reporting a plain nonnegative integer count of locked satellites, not a packed GPS-status value. Warn below satellites 8 Warns when the satellite count is strictly below this value. Nonnegative integers, steps of 1. Requires Satellite count source . Critical below satellites 4 Critical alarm when the satellite count is strictly below this value. Nonnegative integers, steps of 1; must not exceed Warn below satellites . Requires Satellite count source . Show tape off Replaces bearing text with a scrolling direction tape where space permits. Bearing format degrees degrees shows numeric azimuth; quadrant shows notation such as N29°E . Shown only when Show tape is off. Show coordinates off Shows the model's latitude and longitude where space permits, independently of Show tape . Show satellites on Shows the satellite icon and locked-satellite count in the header where space permits. Requires Satellite count source ; turning it off does not disable satellite alerts. Accent cyan Color used for the normal state: cyan , green , amber , or orange . Alarm and stale states use the shared state colors instead. Behavior Distance from home is always the main reading. It uses metres or kilometres according to distance. Zero latitude and longitude together mean no fix, matching EdgeTX's uninitialized GPS values. A valid 0m reading means the model is at home, not that GPS is unavailable. Satellite count and alerts With Satellite count source selected, Show satellites controls the satellite icon and locked-satellite count in the header. It defaults to on, including for existing layouts without this setting. Turning it off hides both the icon and count, not the warning, critical, missing-source, or stale indications. The indicator is also hidden when it cannot fit; alerts remain active. With no source selected, neither the indicator nor satellite alerts appear. The defaults make 0 critical, 4 warning, and 8 normal. Thresholds do not control home capture, and distance never triggers an alarm. First-arm home With Home position set to edgetx , home comes from EdgeTX. Selecting first-arm captures a separate AeroGrid home without changing EdgeTX home or the flight controller's return-home position. It uses Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings , falling back to an existing panel switch only before model arming has been saved. Saving None disables first-arm capture rather than restoring the fallback. Older layouts with a home arm switch retain first-arm behavior; those without one retain EdgeTX home. AeroGrid must observe disarmed, then armed; opening the widget already armed does not capture home. With an effective armed switch, AeroGrid captures the home position when the model is first armed. If that capture fails, each later disarm and re-arm tries again until home is set. A captured home or failed attempt survives telemetry loss, panel recreation, and layout or theme reloads in this widget instance. Panels using the same GPS source and armed switch share the capture. A different pair has its own capture. Home is not saved to disk: restarting the radio, reloading the model, or removing and recreating the widget starts a new session. Separate widget instances have independent homes. Changing the model's Arm switch clears retained AeroGrid homes on every dashboard. The Session reset switch also clears these homes; observe a new disarm/arm transition to capture again. EdgeTX home is unchanged. To investigate HOME NOT SET , first add a Host diagnostics panel and select its log section on any AeroGrid screen. The shared in-memory log records captured/missed or switch unavailable, together with the inputs used for the decision: current time, availability, freshness, stale state, value, update time, reported delay, and coordinate validity. These are GPS inputs for capture attempts, or switch inputs for switch-unavailable events. Times are 10 ms ticks; GPS delay is seconds. Poll age is now - updatedAt ; combined age is delay * 100 + now - updatedAt . Missing values appear as nil . No coordinates are logged. The capture gates and first-transition-only timing are unchanged. The log cannot recover an attempt made before logging was enabled; reproduce it in a new widget session. See Host diagnostics for retention settings and the fullscreen history viewer. Bearing display Show tape places the tape below distance in square and tall panels, and beside it in wide panels. Resizing updates this arrangement. It spans 210 degrees beneath a fixed pointer, with N , E , S , and W labels, major ticks every 30 degrees, and minor ticks every 10 degrees. Its tint follows the panel state. When bearing is unavailable, the tape shows the reason instead of a pointer and scale that could imply due north. With Show tape off, Bearing format selects numeric azimuth or quadrant notation. Bearing text and Show coordinates are displayed only where they fit; a tape that cannot fit yields to distance. Stale data retains the last bearing with the panel's STALE indication. Location details In fullscreen, tap the panel to open a QR code linking to Google Maps at the model's GPS coordinates, not home. The code and coordinates are frozen when opened; close and reopen for a newer position. A stale fix is marked LAST KNOWN POSITION . Without a valid position, tapping does nothing. Tap anywhere or press RTN/Back/Exit to return. Location details are unavailable outside fullscreen and while editing. The radio generates the QR code without a network connection; following it on a phone uses Google Maps. When bearing is unavailable, the tape shows the reason instead of a pointer and scale that could imply due north. With Show tape off, Bearing format selects numeric azimuth or quadrant notation. Bearing text and Show coordinates are displayed only where they fit; a tape that cannot fit yields to distance. Stale data retains the last bearing with the panel's STALE indication.

docs.text: In fullscreen, tap the panel to open a QR code linking to Google Maps at the model's GPS coordinates, not home. The code and coordinates are frozen when opened; close and reopen for a newer position. A stale fix is marked LAST KNOWN POSITION . Without a valid position, tapping does nothing. Tap anywhere or press RTN/Back/Exit to return. Location details are unavailable outside fullscreen and while editing. The radio generates the QR code without a network connection; following it on a phone uses Google Maps.

docs.text: RX battery 1x2 2x1 2x2 Displays aircraft-battery voltage from an EdgeTX cells monitor or a numeric pack-voltage source such as RxBt . The source must measure the flight battery; regulated receiver supply voltage does not reveal pack voltage. The headline shows two decimals, not a promise of sensor accuracy or resolution. Settings Setting Default What it does Label PACK Panel heading. Voltage source Cels EdgeTX source supplying individual cells or total pack voltage. The panel detects which kind of reading it receives. Cell count (0 = auto) 0 Series count for a numeric pack source: 0 estimates it; 1 to 16 sets it explicitly. Steps of 1. Cells monitors supply their own count and ignore this setting. Primary reading cell cell shows the lowest monitored cell, or the calculated average for a numeric pack source. pack shows total pack voltage. Voltage levels Per-cell voltage settings. Full (V/cell) 4.2 Full end of the battery or bar scale, and the voltage used to estimate series count. 0 to 10, in steps of 0.01. Shown only when Visualization is battery or bar . Warning (V/cell) 3.6 Warning at or below this per-cell voltage. 0 to 10, in steps of 0.01. Critical (V/cell) 3.4 Critical at or below this per-cell voltage, taking priority over warning. 0 to 10, in steps of 0.01. Empty (V/cell) 3.2 Empty end of the battery or bar scale. 0 to 10, in steps of 0.01. Shown only when Visualization is battery or bar . Visualization battery battery draws a battery glyph; bar draws a voltage bar; details shows readings without either visual. Show alt reading on Requests pack voltage when Primary reading is cell , or average cell voltage when it is pack . Shown only when Visualization is bar or details . Show cell count on Requests the measured, configured, or estimated series count. Shown only when Visualization is bar or details . Show cell delta off Requests highest minus lowest individual cell voltage. Only a cells monitor with no rejected cell readings can supply it. Shown only when Visualization is bar or details . Accent cyan Color used for the normal state: cyan , green , amber , or orange . Alarm and stale states use the shared state colors instead. Behavior A cells monitor supplies its own count and pack sum. Alarms judge the lowest valid cell, even when Primary reading is pack . Invalid cell entries are excluded from the sum and count; Show cell delta supplies no reading if any entries were rejected. A numeric source supplies total pack voltage. The panel divides it by Cell count (0 = auto) to calculate average cell voltage. With an automatic count, the first fresh, valid voltage is divided by Full (V/cell) and rounded to the nearest integer. That estimate is held as voltage falls; after stale or missing data, the next fresh reading starts a new estimate. The Session reset switch also clears the estimate, which is then recalculated from fresh voltage. The count is marked EST , shortened to ~ or omitted when space is tight. Estimation assumes the first reading is near full. A partly charged pack, load sag, starting mid-flight, or a different chemistry can give the wrong count. Set the known series count when possible. Pack voltage cannot reveal a weak or unbalanced cell, so alarms judge only its calculated average. All four voltage levels are in volts per cell. Full (V/cell) must be above Warning (V/cell) , which must be at or above Critical (V/cell) , which must be at or above Empty (V/cell) . These constraints still apply when Visualization is details . Thresholds include the boundary value, and critical takes priority. The battery and bar are empty at Empty (V/cell) and full at Full (V/cell) . For a pack headline, fill uses average cell voltage; for a monitored cell headline, it uses the lowest cell. This is voltage headroom, not remaining capacity. Values outside the range keep the visual empty or full while the number still shows the actual voltage. Visualization and details battery never shows supporting readings. bar and details show enabled, available details only when they fit: cell count has priority over cell delta, which has priority over the alternate reading. Both a footer and a side stack are tried before details are dropped. If delta cannot fit, a shorter alternate reading can still use the remaining room. Show cell delta displays the difference to two decimals with a delta symbol. Show alt reading displays pack voltage to one decimal, or average cell voltage to two decimals. Captions shorten when needed. Small panels may retain only the headline; enlarging the panel restores details when they fit. States Condition Presentation Fresh judged voltage above the warning threshold Reading and visual in their normal colors. Judged voltage at or below Warning (V/cell) Amber state color, tinted panel, WARN badge. Judged voltage at or below Critical (V/cell) Red state color, tinted panel, CRIT badge; critical takes priority. Retained reading becomes stale Last voltage retained, muted presentation, STALE badge. No usable headline -- , no unit or battery glyph, N/A badge. Empty cells table NO CELLS in the count slot when it fits in bar or details . No valid cells, or a malformed nonnumeric reading CELLS ERR in the count slot when it fits in bar or details . Invalid numeric pack voltage or unusable series count VOLT ERR in the count slot when it fits in bar or details . No reading has arrived Count row is blank. Error wordings use the count slot even when Show cell count is off.

docs.text: Service probe Displays label-and-value rows from one shared AeroGrid data service. This developer diagnostic panel helps check normalized values, units, precision, availability, and navigation calculations independently of the flight panels that use them. The panel needs at least 2x2 cells to fit its rows. Settings Setting Default What it does Label service name Panel heading. Clear it to use the selected Service . Service telemetry Service to inspect: telemetry , model , control , extrema , or navigation . Source none EdgeTX source picker. Select the reading for telemetry , GPS source for navigation , trim source for control , or reading to track for extrema . Unused by model . Second source none Legacy arm switch condition for extrema , used only before model arming is saved. Enter a physical position or logical switch name, not a numeric source. Unused by the other services. Index 0 Zero-based timer index for model (0 to 2) or global variable index for control (0 to 8). Unused by the other services. The number control steps by 1 from -100000 to 100000, not just the useful index range, and has no empty option. Accent cyan Panel accent: cyan , green , amber , or orange . Reported service states do not change the panel color. Remove panel Deletes the panel from the screen. All settings remain visible for every Service , including those it does not use. Behavior telemetry reports the selected source name, state, formatted value, unit, precision, reading age, and link status. navigation reports the GPS source, fix and home availability, latitude, longitude, distance, and bearing. model requests model identity, flight mode, transmitter voltage, and the selected timer. control requests the selected trim, when Source is not empty, and the selected global variable in the current flight mode. extrema requests shared flight-session status and, when Source is not empty, session minimum and maximum values for that source. These three services report shared subscriptions, so rows requested by other panels can appear too. For extrema , the Arm switch in Model settings takes precedence over Second source . Consumers with the same effective switch share session data; without an arm condition, tracking is open-ended. The model's Session reset switch clears these session extrema and timing. This is diagnostic session tracking, not shared flight detection. Rows are left-aligned in two columns and refresh about twice per second. Only the rows that fit are shown, up to eight. Enlarge the panel to reveal more; any remaining rows are omitted. Service state text is diagnostic output, not a panel alarm or stale badge. States Condition Presentation Service available The service's diagnostic rows with the normal Accent . Telemetry reading stale or unavailable State and value reported in the diagnostic rows; panel colors remain normal. No navigation fix or home NO in the corresponding rows; missing coordinates, distance, or bearing show - . Model or control reading unavailable N/A or the service's unavailable timer text in the affected row. No tracked extrema available N/A in the affected source row; flight and arming status remain separate rows. Service missing Uppercase service name with UNAVAILABLE ; no unavailable badge. Subscription fails Empty report area; the panel does not display the subscription error. Service returns no rows Empty report area beneath the heading. Report exceeds available space Trailing rows are hidden; no warning badge is added.

docs.text: Trim 1x2 2x1 2x2 Displays the radio's effective aileron, elevator, and rudder trim positions, including values inherited from another flight mode. The panel is read-only; use the radio's trim controls to change a trim. No aircraft telemetry is needed. Settings Setting Default What it does Label TRIM Panel heading. Trim 1 trim-ail Trim source shown as aileron on the top bar. Enter its EdgeTX source name as text, such as trim-ail . Trim 2 trim-ele Trim source shown as elevator on the left bar. Enter its EdgeTX source name as text, such as trim-ele . Trim 4 trim-rud Trim source shown as rudder on the bottom bar. Enter its EdgeTX source name as text, such as trim-rud . Scale auto auto starts with standard travel and widens to extended travel when needed. standard or extended keeps the range fixed. Readout percent percent shows signed percentages; raw shows stored trim units; none hides numeric readouts. Detected three-position trims show named positions instead of numbers. Accent cyan Panel accent: cyan , green , amber , or orange . Available trim fills stay green. Behavior Aileron is the top bar, elevator the left bar, and rudder the bottom bar. Fill extends from neutral toward the current trim. The white dot shows the combined aileron/elevator position and disappears if either source is unavailable. Source names can change, but the positions and A , E , and R readout suffixes retain their assigned roles. Readout uses percentages of the selected scale, or stored trim units for raw . Standard travel is ±128 stored units; extended travel is ±512. auto widens each trim's scale once a non-three-position reading exceeds standard travel, and keeps that wider scale even when the trim returns toward center. A fixed scale clips the visual at its ends without changing the raw readout. Three-position trims show 3P MID , 3P HI , or 3P LO . Detection requires observing both center and full deflection without intermediate positions; a single end-stop reading cannot distinguish a normal trim from a toggle. docs.text: YAML reference This page is the complete layout-file reference for people writing AeroGrid layouts by hand, often with an AI agent. Use it to produce a file that the widget can load; for what each option means in the on-radio settings drawer, see the relevant panel page (each panel section below links to its own page). Panel setting keys are documented here only. File locations AeroGrid reads YAML layout files from two places: Bundled layouts: /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/<name>.yaml . User layouts: /AEROGRID/layouts/<name>.yaml (on the SD card). A user layout with the selected name takes precedence over a bundled layout of the same name. The user folder is outside the widget folder, so a widget update does not replace user layouts. The editor accepts names of 1–24 letters, digits, _ or - ; Empty is reserved for the blank screen. Use that name as the filename stem. If loading a candidate fails, AeroGrid can try its backup, the bundled file of that name, then the bundled default and its backup. Document structure A new layout should use version 5 and exactly a 4 × 4 grid. col and row are zero-based; spans count grid cells. The cell at the upper left is (0, 0) . Top-level key Type Required Meaning version integer yes Layout schema version. Write 5 . grid mapping yes Must contain columns: 4 and rows: 4 . Other grid dimensions are rejected. panels sequence of mappings yes Ordered panel placements. Use [] for an empty layout. session mapping no Dashboard-wide flight-session options; see Session . theme mapping no Not supported. A layout that has this key is reported as invalid. Choose a theme in widget settings instead. Each panels entry has these placement keys: Key Type Required Rule id string yes Unique within the layout; letters, digits, _ and - only ( ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ). type string yes Panel kind, using the exact names in the Panels sections below. It must also contain only letters, digits, _ and - . col integer yes Starting column, 0–3. row integer yes Starting row, 0–3. colSpan integer yes Positive width in cells; must fit within column 4 and be supported by the panel. rowSpan integer yes Positive height in cells; must fit within row 4 and be supported by the panel. config mapping no Panel-specific settings. Omit it to use panel defaults; otherwise write a mapping, not a sequence or scalar. A placement must fit the 4 × 4 grid: col + colSpan <= 4 and row + rowSpan <= 4 . Placements may touch edges but may not occupy the same cell. If two placements overlap, the first valid placement in the sequence wins and the later one is dropped. A panel must also support its exact span, written as <colSpan>x<rowSpan> (for example, 2x1 ); the word any in a panel's span list accepts every in-bounds span. Panel IDs and types are case-sensitive. Unknown top-level keys and extra placement keys are preserved rather than rejected. In contrast, a key inside config that the panel does not declare is reported as an unknown setting; spelling and case must match exactly. Session session is optional and must be a mapping when present. Its only declared key is armSource ; unknown session keys are not reported and are not retained in the normalized session: Key Type Default Meaning armSource string unset Legacy physical-position or logical-switch fallback for flight-session extrema before model arming has been saved. Numeric sources such as sa or ch5 are no longer supported: select a model switch instead. Without either condition, extrema maintain an open-ended session. Configure Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings , not in layout YAML. It is saved once per model and overrides session.armSource and panel armSwitch values on every dashboard. Before model arming is saved, each consumer retains its own nonblank legacy switch; differing legacy settings are allowed, but conflicting flight detector proposals stop new flight detection. Existing panel arm fields are shown only while their fallback is active; overridden values survive layout Save. Saving None disables arming model-wide, not restoring fallbacks. Old widget Armed selections are not automatically imported or used to guess a model condition. Custom State conditions remain independent. Session reset switch and flight detection/output are also Model settings , not layout keys. Validation and errors The loader parses and validates a candidate before building panels. Unsupported YAML syntax, an unsupported schema version, a missing or non-4×4 grid, a non-sequence panels value, or the unsupported layout-level theme key makes the candidate invalid; AeroGrid reports the load problem and may recover using the next backup or bundled candidate. Versions 1–4 are migrated to version 5 in memory. Existing panel, Navigation, and legacy arm settings are retained. Version 4 detection settings remain available for migration to Model settings. Save writes version 5 without deleting retained legacy arm conditions. Write version 5 for new files. An invalid panel entry is rejected without preventing other valid entries from loading. This includes a non-mapping entry, an unsafe or duplicate ID, an unknown panel type, invalid placement values, a placement outside the grid, an overlap, or a span the panel does not support. The failed panel is dropped and its reason is reported. When overlaps occur, the earlier accepted entry remains. For a top-level setting, a missing or wrong-typed value falls back to its declared default (or remains unset if it has no default). A string outside a setting's declared choice list also falls back to its default. These issues are reported with the panel ID; they do not by themselves drop the panel. Nested list-entry fields are not generically defaulted or type-checked by the settings resolver: panel-specific validation reports malformed nested values instead. Panel-specific cross-field checks may also report warnings. During normal display these are reported while loading and the host attempts to build the panel; if the panel rejects the settings during construction, that panel is dropped. An editor preview rejects a panel as soon as any warning is found. Ranges and steps listed in the panel tables are checked only by the on-radio editor: an out-of-range or off-step value loads and displays, but the editor refuses to save the layout until it is corrected. For reliable authoring, correct every warning rather than relying on fallback behavior. Unknown config keys are kept in the resolved configuration but reported as “is not a setting of this panel”; they are not silently discarded. This catches typos. A non-mapping config is normalized to an empty mapping, so always use the mapping form. Unknown top-level keys and extra panel-entry keys are retained without a setting warning; do not rely on them having meaning to this version of AeroGrid. YAML parsing and structural validation do not prove that an EdgeTX source exists on a particular model or radio. Use exact source names as the radio reports them. A missing live source can still render as unavailable even when the layout structure is valid. YAML syntax supported The widget uses a deliberately small YAML parser, not a general YAML implementation. Emit only these forms: Indented block mappings ( key: value ) and sequences ( - item ), using two spaces per indentation level . Tabs and odd-space indentation are errors. Strings, numbers, lowercase true and false , and null or ~ scalars. To force a string that looks like a number, boolean, or null, quote it. Single-quoted strings; represent an apostrophe inside one as '' . Double-quoted strings support \\ , \" , \n , \r and \t escapes. Comments beginning with # at the start of a line or after whitespace. A # inside a quoted string is preserved. Empty flow collections only: [] and {} . They are useful for empty sequences and mappings; non-empty inline collections are unsupported. Empty mapping values with indented children, including nested mappings and lists. Do not use anchors or aliases, tags, block scalars ( | or > ), flow-style non-empty lists or maps, merge keys, directives, or other general YAML features. Duplicate mapping keys are rejected. Mapping keys must begin with an ASCII letter or _ , and may then contain letters, digits, _ or - . Quote text that could otherwise be parsed as a boolean, number or null. Prefer double-quoting source names, labels and other strings when uncertain. Panels Omitted settings use their listed defaults. “Unset” means the setting has no schema default and stays unset unless specified. Numeric constraints in the tables are the drawer's declared bounds/steps or, when explicitly noted, the panel's runtime validation. All choice values are the YAML values, even if the drawer displays a friendlier choice label. chart Use a separate Chart panel for recorded telemetry, not a live Metric sparkline. It supports 2x1, 3x1, 4x1, 2x2, 3x2, 4x2, 3x3, 4x3, and 4x4. Key Values and defaults label Optional title; omitted or empty hides the title and reclaims header space for the plot. armSwitch Legacy physical-position or logical-switch fallback, blank by default. Used and shown only before model arming has been saved. With neither condition, recording is disabled. metrics Contiguous list of zero to three numeric sources. Empty is valid for editor setup. source , unit , precision Per-metric source name, optional unit override, and integer precision 0–3 (default sensor precision). accent Per-metric trace color or panel stripe: cyan, green, orange, amber. Traces default to cyan, orange, green in order. Modern Light renders the cyan trace with blue ink. rangeMin , rangeMax Optional per-metric finite bounds. Omit either key for Auto on that side; zero is an explicit bound. If both are set, maximum must exceed minimum. Shared scales use the lowest configured minimum and highest configured maximum; a side with no configured bound follows all recorded series automatically. timeRange growing (default) or rolling . duration 30s , 1m (default), 2m , 5m , 10m . Fixed Rolling window; ignored in Growing mode. scaling shared (default) or independent . Select independent explicitly for unlike units. range Obsolete preview setting ( auto / fixed ), accepted for compatibility but ignored. Only the presence of rangeMin / rangeMax determines fixed versus automatic bounds. smoothing off (default), light , medium , strong ; line-only EMA with approximately 0.5/1/2-second response. Each metric also accepts label . The title is above the shared plot, with each metric's name/value and raw min/max grouped in a right-hand legend. Automatic bounds use raw lifetime recorded extrema with padding and rounding. For example, rangeMin: 0 with no rangeMax anchors the bottom at zero and automatically adjusts the top; omit both keys for a fully automatic range. Set Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings ; changes save automatically. A retained panel armSwitch is used only before model arming has been saved. A qualified shared flight with the same effective arm condition keeps recording through disarm grace until confirmed flight end. Otherwise disarming pauses immediately. Rearming during grace does not break or duplicate a flight; rearming after a pause resumes the same history with a gap and dotted connectors. The horizontal axis counts cumulative recording time, including retained grace samples. Neutral background bands show actual flight times; bottom-axis triangles mark arming and disarming except the first arming. No logical-switch output or Flight counter panel is needed. Growing starts at one minute and expands to the next whole minute when exceeded; its duration is not configurable. Rolling keeps only the latest plot window but retains raw lifetime min/max. History is RAM-only and clears on dashboard reload or model-wide session reset. Connected linear compression bounds error to half a step of each metric's precision (sensor precision when omitted); with smoothing, this bound applies to the filtered signal. Each distinct source/options recording holds 6,144 knots, covering at least 10 minutes at 10 Hz even without compression savings. docs.text: This page is the complete layout-file reference for people writing AeroGrid layouts by hand, often with an AI agent. Use it to produce a file that the widget can load; for what each option means in the on-radio settings drawer, see the relevant panel page (each panel section below links to its own page). Panel setting keys are documented here only.
docs.title: YAML reference

docs.text: AeroGrid reads YAML layout files from two places: Bundled layouts: /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/<name>.yaml . User layouts: /AEROGRID/layouts/<name>.yaml (on the SD card). A user layout with the selected name takes precedence over a bundled layout of the same name. The user folder is outside the widget folder, so a widget update does not replace user layouts. The editor accepts names of 1–24 letters, digits, _ or - ; Empty is reserved for the blank screen. Use that name as the filename stem. If loading a candidate fails, AeroGrid can try its backup, the bundled file of that name, then the bundled default and its backup.
docs.title: File locations

docs.text: A new layout should use version 5 and exactly a 4 × 4 grid. col and row are zero-based; spans count grid cells. The cell at the upper left is (0, 0) . Top-level key Type Required Meaning version integer yes Layout schema version. Write 5 . grid mapping yes Must contain columns: 4 and rows: 4 . Other grid dimensions are rejected. panels sequence of mappings yes Ordered panel placements. Use [] for an empty layout. session mapping no Dashboard-wide flight-session options; see Session . theme mapping no Not supported. A layout that has this key is reported as invalid. Choose a theme in widget settings instead. Each panels entry has these placement keys: Key Type Required Rule id string yes Unique within the layout; letters, digits, _ and - only ( ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ). type string yes Panel kind, using the exact names in the Panels sections below. It must also contain only letters, digits, _ and - . col integer yes Starting column, 0–3. row integer yes Starting row, 0–3. colSpan integer yes Positive width in cells; must fit within column 4 and be supported by the panel. rowSpan integer yes Positive height in cells; must fit within row 4 and be supported by the panel. config mapping no Panel-specific settings. Omit it to use panel defaults; otherwise write a mapping, not a sequence or scalar. A placement must fit the 4 × 4 grid: col + colSpan <= 4 and row + rowSpan <= 4 . Placements may touch edges but may not occupy the same cell. If two placements overlap, the first valid placement in the sequence wins and the later one is dropped. A panel must also support its exact span, written as <colSpan>x<rowSpan> (for example, 2x1 ); the word any in a panel's span list accepts every in-bounds span. Panel IDs and types are case-sensitive. Unknown top-level keys and extra placement keys are preserved rather than rejected. In contrast, a key inside config that the panel does not declare is reported as an unknown setting; spelling and case must match exactly.

docs.text: The loader parses and validates a candidate before building panels. Unsupported YAML syntax, an unsupported schema version, a missing or non-4×4 grid, a non-sequence panels value, or the unsupported layout-level theme key makes the candidate invalid; AeroGrid reports the load problem and may recover using the next backup or bundled candidate. Versions 1–4 are migrated to version 5 in memory. Existing panel, Navigation, and legacy arm settings are retained. Version 4 detection settings remain available for migration to Model settings. Save writes version 5 without deleting retained legacy arm conditions. Write version 5 for new files. An invalid panel entry is rejected without preventing other valid entries from loading. This includes a non-mapping entry, an unsafe or duplicate ID, an unknown panel type, invalid placement values, a placement outside the grid, an overlap, or a span the panel does not support. The failed panel is dropped and its reason is reported. When overlaps occur, the earlier accepted entry remains. For a top-level setting, a missing or wrong-typed value falls back to its declared default (or remains unset if it has no default). A string outside a setting's declared choice list also falls back to its default. These issues are reported with the panel ID; they do not by themselves drop the panel. Nested list-entry fields are not generically defaulted or type-checked by the settings resolver: panel-specific validation reports malformed nested values instead. Panel-specific cross-field checks may also report warnings. During normal display these are reported while loading and the host attempts to build the panel; if the panel rejects the settings during construction, that panel is dropped. An editor preview rejects a panel as soon as any warning is found. Ranges and steps listed in the panel tables are checked only by the on-radio editor: an out-of-range or off-step value loads and displays, but the editor refuses to save the layout until it is corrected. For reliable authoring, correct every warning rather than relying on fallback behavior. Unknown config keys are kept in the resolved configuration but reported as “is not a setting of this panel”; they are not silently discarded. This catches typos. A non-mapping config is normalized to an empty mapping, so always use the mapping form. Unknown top-level keys and extra panel-entry keys are retained without a setting warning; do not rely on them having meaning to this version of AeroGrid. YAML parsing and structural validation do not prove that an EdgeTX source exists on a particular model or radio. Use exact source names as the radio reports them. A missing live source can still render as unavailable even when the layout structure is valid.
docs.title: Validation and errors

docs.text: The widget uses a deliberately small YAML parser, not a general YAML implementation. Emit only these forms: Indented block mappings ( key: value ) and sequences ( - item ), using two spaces per indentation level . Tabs and odd-space indentation are errors. Strings, numbers, lowercase true and false , and null or ~ scalars. To force a string that looks like a number, boolean, or null, quote it. Single-quoted strings; represent an apostrophe inside one as '' . Double-quoted strings support \\ , \" , \n , \r and \t escapes. Comments beginning with # at the start of a line or after whitespace. A # inside a quoted string is preserved. Empty flow collections only: [] and {} . They are useful for empty sequences and mappings; non-empty inline collections are unsupported. Empty mapping values with indented children, including nested mappings and lists. Do not use anchors or aliases, tags, block scalars ( | or > ), flow-style non-empty lists or maps, merge keys, directives, or other general YAML features. Duplicate mapping keys are rejected. Mapping keys must begin with an ASCII letter or _ , and may then contain letters, digits, _ or - . Quote text that could otherwise be parsed as a boolean, number or null. Prefer double-quoting source names, labels and other strings when uncertain.

Numeric constraints in the tables are the drawer's declared bounds/steps or, when explicitly noted, the panel's runtime validation. All choice values are the YAML values, even if the drawer displays a friendlier choice label.

docs.text: Use a separate Chart panel for recorded telemetry, not a live Metric sparkline. It supports 2x1, 3x1, 4x1, 2x2, 3x2, 4x2, 3x3, 4x3, and 4x4. Key Values and defaults label Optional title; omitted or empty hides the title and reclaims header space for the plot. armSwitch Legacy physical-position or logical-switch fallback, blank by default. Used and shown only before model arming has been saved. With neither condition, recording is disabled. metrics Contiguous list of zero to three numeric sources. Empty is valid for editor setup. source , unit , precision Per-metric source name, optional unit override, and integer precision 0–3 (default sensor precision). accent Per-metric trace color or panel stripe: cyan, green, orange, amber. Traces default to cyan, orange, green in order. Modern Light renders the cyan trace with blue ink. rangeMin , rangeMax Optional per-metric finite bounds. Omit either key for Auto on that side; zero is an explicit bound. If both are set, maximum must exceed minimum. Shared scales use the lowest configured minimum and highest configured maximum; a side with no configured bound follows all recorded series automatically. timeRange growing (default) or rolling . duration 30s , 1m (default), 2m , 5m , 10m . Fixed Rolling window; ignored in Growing mode. scaling shared (default) or independent . Select independent explicitly for unlike units. range Obsolete preview setting ( auto / fixed ), accepted for compatibility but ignored. Only the presence of rangeMin / rangeMax determines fixed versus automatic bounds. smoothing off (default), light , medium , strong ; line-only EMA with approximately 0.5/1/2-second response. Each metric also accepts label . The title is above the shared plot, with each metric's name/value and raw min/max grouped in a right-hand legend. Automatic bounds use raw lifetime recorded extrema with padding and rounding. For example, rangeMin: 0 with no rangeMax anchors the bottom at zero and automatically adjusts the top; omit both keys for a fully automatic range. Set Arm switch in AeroGrid → Model settings ; changes save automatically. A retained panel armSwitch is used only before model arming has been saved. A qualified shared flight with the same effective arm condition keeps recording through disarm grace until confirmed flight end. Otherwise disarming pauses immediately. Rearming during grace does not break or duplicate a flight; rearming after a pause resumes the same history with a gap and dotted connectors. The horizontal axis counts cumulative recording time, including retained grace samples. Neutral background bands show actual flight times; bottom-axis triangles mark arming and disarming except the first arming. No logical-switch output or Flight counter panel is needed. Growing starts at one minute and expands to the next whole minute when exceeded; its duration is not configurable. Rolling keeps only the latest plot window but retains raw lifetime min/max. History is RAM-only and clears on dashboard reload or model-wide session reset. Connected linear compression bounds error to half a step of each metric's precision (sensor precision when omitted); with smoothing, this bound applies to the filtered signal. Each distinct source/options recording holds 6,144 knots, covering at least 10 minutes at 10 Hz even without compression savings. At capacity, HISTORY FULL preserves existing plot history and stops new plot samples, but raw readouts/extrema keep updating. Rolling mode reuses expired storage. No older data is recompressed more loosely. Recordings share history only when their armed switch, source, and recording options match. version: 5 grid: columns: 4 rows: 4 panels: - id: power-chart type: chart col: 0 row: 0 colSpan: 4 rowSpan: 2 config: label: Power timeRange: growing scaling: independent smoothing: light metrics: - source: RxBt label: RX precision: 1 accent: cyan - source: Curr label: A precision: 1 accent: green

docs.text: Add a dashboard Watch the dashboard setup walkthrough on YouTube . Add AeroGrid to a radio screen and choose a layout. Install AeroGrid first and select the model you want to use. Add a screen Open the main screen's top-left menu and choose UI Setup . Select the + tab, then tap Add Screen . On the new screen, tap the Layout thumbnail and choose App mode . This makes one widget fill the screen. Tap Setup widgets , then tap the empty widget area. Choose AeroGrid in Select widget . In the AeroGrid settings, choose Layout . Select Empty to build your own dashboard, or Default to start with the bundled aircraft dashboard. Choose Modern Dark or Modern Light for Theme . Press RTN to close the settings and leave setup. Your dashboard is now on the new screen. Repeat these steps to add another dashboard. In fullscreen, tap AeroGrid → Model settings and set Arm switch to the physical position or logical switch that means armed. Changes save automatically across the model's dashboards. Arming is not a widget option beside Layout and Theme. See Model settings for shared arming, flight detection, session reset, and the flight-status output used with your own sounds. Understand layouts A dashboard is AeroGrid on a radio screen. A layout defines its panels, their positions and sizes, and their settings, including sources and alarms. Choose a layout to decide what that dashboard displays. Layout Purpose Empty A blank starting point for your own dashboard. Shows instructions until you start editing. Default A ready-made aircraft dashboard. Configure its sources, switches, battery cell count, and alarms for your model before using it. Diagnostics A diagnostics dashboard for checking loaded components and errors. Palette Fixed theme samples: color tokens, text, bars, a dial, and every panel state. Not flight data. Bundled layouts are stored in /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/layouts/ . Your saved layouts are stored separately in /AEROGRID/layouts/ , so upgrading AeroGrid leaves them untouched. Save updates the current layout. For a bundled layout it creates your copy in /AEROGRID/layouts/ under the same name, leaving the bundled original untouched. Save as... creates a separately named layout. Several dashboards, even on different models, can select the same layout. They share all panel settings, so check that the sources and switches suit each model. Saving changes under that name affects all dashboards using it when they next reload. Restart the radio after saving a new name so it appears in the Layout picker. A missing layout falls back to Default . App mode and Full screen Layout What you see App mode A dashboard covering the display, without the EdgeTX top bar, flight-mode label, sliders, or trims. The menu button remains in the top-left corner. Full screen ( 1 x 1 ) One dashboard widget, with the option to keep EdgeTX's top bar, flight-mode label, sliders, and trims. Use App mode for a clean dashboard, or Full screen to keep the radio's standard information alongside it. In App mode, a wider top-left panel leaves more room beside the menu button. To arrange and configure panels, continue with Edit a dashboard on the radio . For palette settings, see Customize themes .

docs.text: Customize themes Choose a theme Choose Theme in the widget settings. Mode Behavior Modern Dark AeroGrid's dark instrument palette. Modern Light Pale instrument panels, dark text, and light-background accents and alarm tints. Modern Dark palette. Modern Light palette with dark text and light-background alarm tints. Theme files and previews Themes are stored as individual .yml files. Shipped themes live in /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/themes/ ; add user themes to /AEROGRID/themes/ . Theme names are the filename stems, and user files override shipped files with the same name. AeroGrid updates the Theme picker registry automatically; do not edit /AEROGRID/theme-registry.txt . Use the Palette layout to preview palettes against fixed samples before applying one to a dashboard. Select Palette as the layout on a separate App-mode screen. It shows the actual AeroGrid theme and rendering primitives with fixed sample data, without a receiver or telemetry setup. Switch the widget's Theme option between Modern Dark and Modern Light to compare the same samples. Normal, active, warning, critical, stale, and unavailable cards are shown together. Create a custom theme Copy one complete file from /WIDGETS/AeroGrid/themes/ to /AEROGRID/themes/<name>.yml . Set name to the filename stem and provide a label and version: 1 . Define every color token and spacing value; themes do not inherit from one another. Colors use 0xRRGGBB , such as 0xFFFFFF for white and 0x000000 for black. accent selects the default semantic accent ( cyan , green , amber , or orange ). Put all color values, including optional warningBg , criticalBg , and activeBg panel-surface backgrounds, in the colors: section. light and tintSeparation tune light-theme alert surfaces. correctForContrast controls automatic legibility adjustments; it defaults to true . Set it to false to preserve all explicitly specified palette values, including warningBg , criticalBg , and activeBg , without contrast-based substitution. You are responsible for readability in this mode. Omitted alert backgrounds still use contrast-checked derived tints, and invalid theme values are still rejected. Use spaces for YAML indentation, not tabs. With contrast correction enabled, safeguards may adjust a color to preserve legibility. Review the palette on the Palette layout and on the radio as well as in the simulator. Restart the radio or simulator after adding a theme so the picker reloads. Chart colors Optional colors.chartCyan , chartGreen , chartAmber , and chartOrange override Chart trace and legend-name colors without changing other panels or alarm accents. colors.chartGrid sets the minute grid and time baseline. When omitted, the chart inks use their corresponding semantic accents and the grid uses border , preserving existing custom themes. Modern Light supplies stronger chart inks and a quiet neutral-gray grid. With contrast correction enabled, explicit chart inks are adjusted to at least 4.5:1 contrast against the panel surface; the grid remains the configured color.

docs.text: Edit a dashboard on the radio Watch the panel editing walkthrough on YouTube . Add a dashboard first, then customize its panels on the radio. Long-press the dashboard to enter fullscreen. The native EdgeTX menu stays unchanged in App mode; fullscreen shows a same-sized AeroGrid icon instead. Tap AeroGrid → UI setup to start editing, even on an Empty dashboard. You can also long-press a panel again. Enter also starts editing. A gear icon appears in the top-right corner of each panel. AeroGrid → Model settings opens shared model settings without entering layout edit mode. Changes save automatically, independently of layout Save/Save as... . The host menu is hidden while editing so it does not cover panel resize corners. See Model settings for shared arming, flight detection, flight-status output, and the Session reset switch. Session reset preserves unsaved layout edits and does not close an open Model settings page. Action How Add Tap the + panel , then choose a panel type. Its settings open automatically. Move Drag the panel's body to a free position. Reorder Drag onto another panel. Compatible panels exchange positions or order; other panels stay put. Resize Drag the top-left, bottom-left, or bottom-right corner. The opposite corner stays fixed. Configure Tap the gear in the top-right corner. Remove Open the gear, then choose Remove panel . Removal is immediate. Panels snap to the 4 × 4 layout grid. Moves and sizes must fit without overlapping other panels. The + panel disappears when there is no free cell. There are no grid lines or resize handles: drag the corners directly. Moving and resizing require touch. Configure panels Use the native choices, toggles, number controls, and text keyboard in the settings dialog. Sources, switches, and timers use EdgeTX pickers. Panel titles use the full header width when no state badge is shown. When a badge appears, only its displayed width and a small gap are set aside. Titles never use a smaller font than their badges; a title that still does not fit is shortened, or hidden if too little room remains. The full title returns when space allows, without moving the title or the panel's reading. Metrics and State entries appear as named rows with a summary of their settings. Tap a row to edit it, or tap the full-width + row to add an entry. In a metric entry, choose Source to change the reading. In a State entry, open a state to edit When , Text , and Background . The first true condition wins. Each entry supports up to three conditions; + appends one at the bottom. Delete and recreate a condition to change its priority. Background choices are normal , active , warning , and critical . The main entry's winning choice sets the whole panel's appearance, including its background, sidebar, text colors, and badge. Supporting entries never change the panel mode. Press RTN or tap outside a dialog to return one level. Changes remain in your draft. If settings cannot be previewed, a Panel preview failed message appears. Open its details to read the full panel-specific explanation, then correct the settings. The short status line clears when the preview succeeds. In Companion's simulator, caught errors also appear in View > Debug Output ( F6 ), with repeated messages suppressed. See Simulator logs and caught errors for console filters and persistent logging. Save or discard changes From the editing dashboard, press RTN . If nothing changed, editing closes. Otherwise choose an action: Action Result Save Updates the current layout and exits editing. Save as... Asks for a name and saves a separate layout. Discard changes Exits editing and restores the saved layout. Save As suggests <model name>-L<number> , using the first unused number starting at 1, such as Sonic-L1 or My-Glider-L1 . You can change the suggestion using letters, digits, - , and _ (at most 24 characters). An existing name requires overwrite confirmation. Press RTN in the name dialog to return to the exit menu without losing your draft. After Save As, restart the radio and select the new name in the widget's Layout setting. The widget cannot change its own settings, so it continues showing its previous layout until you select the new one. Layout picker positions are retained in /AEROGRID/layout-registry.txt . If upgrading an existing installation with /AEROGRID/registry.txt , rename that file to layout-registry.txt before starting the radio to preserve saved Layout selections. Do not edit or reorder its entries. Wait for saving to finish before powering off. A save error keeps your draft so you can retry; the previous saved file is retained as .bak . See Understand layouts for where saved layouts live and how multiple dashboards share them.

Save As suggests <model name>-L<number> , using the first unused number starting at 1, such as Sonic-L1 or My-Glider-L1 . You can change the suggestion using letters, digits, - , and _ (at most 24 characters). An existing name requires overwrite confirmation. Press RTN in the name dialog to return to the exit menu without losing your draft. After Save As, restart the radio and select the new name in the widget's Layout setting. The widget cannot change its own settings, so it continues showing its previous layout until you select the new one. Layout picker positions are retained in /AEROGRID/layout-registry.txt . If upgrading an existing installation with /AEROGRID/registry.txt , rename that file to layout-registry.txt before starting the radio to preserve saved Layout selections. Do not edit or reorder its entries. Wait for saving to finish before powering off. A save error keeps your draft so you can retry; the previous saved file is retained as .bak . See Understand layouts for where saved layouts live and how multiple dashboards share them.
