docs.text: Edit model settings Long-press the AeroGrid dashboard to enter fullscreen. The AeroGrid icon appears in the top-left corner. Tap it, then choose Model settings . Settings apply to every AeroGrid dashboard for the selected model, not to an individual panel or layout. Each confirmed change saves automatically; Back closes the page. Arming Arming tells AeroGrid when your model is armed, using the switch condition you select. It starts Chart recording, captures Navigation's first-arm home, starts flight-session minimum tracking, and enables flight detection. It only observes your model's state; it does not arm the aircraft or control the motor. Setting Default What it does Arm switch none Physical switch position or logical switch (including inverted logical switches) that means armed. Saving None for Arm switch disables arming across all dashboards. Older layouts retain their panel/session arm switches only until model arming is saved. Those legacy controls disappear once model arming takes precedence. Numeric sources such as ch5 or sa are not arm conditions. Flight detection Flight detection distinguishes a flight from simply being armed. It observes the armed condition, motor output, and live telemetry to confirm a flight start, then confirms its end after sustained disarming. Each confirmed start increments the model's flight total once, shown by Flight counter. Detection also supplies Chart flight shading, keeps recording running through the end-detection window, and drives the optional Flight status output for your sounds or announcements. It runs across the model's dashboards even without a Flight counter panel. Setting Default What it does Motor channel CH3 Channel used to measure motor output. Reverse motor off Enable when the motor channel runs from high at idle to low at full power. Motor threshold (%) 25 Motor output must be strictly above this percentage to qualify a flight. Valid values are 0 up to, but not including, 100. Start detection window (s) 30 Continuous armed state, sufficient motor output, and live telemetry required to confirm flight start. End detection window (s) 10 Continuous disarming required to confirm flight end. Rearming within this window keeps the flight open. Smart detection off Also allows sustained altitude or GPS groundspeed evidence to confirm takeoff earlier. See Flight counter . Flight detection observes live telemetry; it does not arm the aircraft. Both detection windows accept values greater than 0 and up to 3600 seconds. Flight timestamps use the beginning of each window, not the later confirmation. Flight status output Flight status switch exposes the detected flight session through a dedicated Sticky logical switch. It turns on when flight start is confirmed and off when flight end is confirmed, including the end-detection window. Session reset also turns it off. Choose None to disable the output. For example, reserve an unused L01 in EdgeTX's Logical Switches page: Switch Function V1 V2 AND switch Delay Duration L01 Sticky unassigned unassigned unassigned 0.0 s 0.0 s Then select L01 as AeroGrid's Flight status switch . The picker lists configured logical switches. AeroGrid controls the switch's state; leave its inputs unassigned and reserve it exclusively for this output. Use L01 in an EdgeTX Special Function to play your chosen sound when a flight starts; use !L01 for an action when it ends. Configure the Special Function's startup and repeat options to avoid unwanted announcements. Do not also use this switch as the Arm switch or Session reset switch, or share it with another script. It is not a safety interlock. Session reset Set Session reset switch to a physical switch position or logical switch. Activation resets the following AeroGrid session data across all dashboards, including hidden screens: Panel or service What resets Chart Recordings, recorded extrema, flight shading, and arm/resume markers. Link status / Extrema Service probe Flight-session minima, maxima, and session timing. Navigation First-arm captured home; a new disarm/arm transition is needed to capture again. RX battery Automatic cell estimate; fresh voltage supplies the next estimate. Flight counter / detection Pending or active detection and its flight-status output, not the flight total. Reset runs once per off-to-on transition, not continuously while held. An input already on at startup, after changing the setting, or after signal recovery does not trigger a reset. Choose None to disable it. Reset during a flight cancels detection without creating a completion. Disarm before another flight can be counted. Flight totals, radio timers, radio telemetry minima/maxima, EdgeTX home, saved settings/layouts, and unsaved editor changes are preserved. Other panels continue showing live data.

docs.text: Troubleshoot and file bugs Troubleshoot a reading If a panel shows no reading or an unexpected value: Open the panel's settings using its gear icon while editing. If it has a Source setting, check that you selected the value you want to display. For a telemetry reading, check that the receiver is connected and the sensor appears on the radio's Telemetry page. Check the guide for that panel for any additional setup: battery , timer , navigation , or metric . A missing reading does not mean the value is zero. Check layouts and themes Use the Diagnostics layout to check loaded components and errors. Check the selected Layout and Theme in the widget settings, and restart the radio or simulator after adding a new layout or theme. Saved files in /AEROGRID/layouts/ and /AEROGRID/themes/ override bundled files with the same name. Check whether an override explains an unexpected layout or color. See Add a dashboard and Customize themes for details. File a bug Search existing issues first. If none describes the problem, open a new issue . Include: Detail What to provide Summary What failed and a specific issue title. Versions AeroGrid package version or Git commit, EdgeTX version, and radio model. Environment Physical radio or simulator; simulator version and desktop OS when relevant. Reproduction Steps, selected layout and theme, and the smallest settings or layout that reproduce the problem. Expected and actual What should happen, what happens instead, and exact error text. Evidence Screenshots, recordings, or relevant diagnostics and logs. Data setup Sources, units, receiver/link state, switches, and timers needed to reproduce it. State whether the issue persists after a restart. Attach a minimal YAML layout, not an entire SD card. Remove private model information, GPS coordinates, and unrelated data before posting. For development-specific diagnostics and contribution guidance, see Issues, changes, and releases .
